scores.why: The yardstick. It is bright, near-monochrome green on black, it still reads as 'the Matrix', and 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px. It is usable, but it has none of the grounded colour or line art the owner asked for.

It carries Signal Box's line language through every page with restraint: a ring and bracket for each page head, the setup track, the fortnight line, To do's timetable track, the Chat thread hanging from Vera's mark, Status rails and the dot under the current page. The lines delimit areas and lead the eye, which is exactly what the owner asked to see again, and it keeps Signal Galley's grounded slate and 0/56 small targets. Faults: it still uses the thick, rounded pewter case the owner criticised, and it has a little more periwinkle than it needs.

It is the first entrant to answer the owner's case critique: thin, square, screwed faceplates. Fine bracket lines with legends set in their breaks give every page one drawn structure. Cyan, the owner's own period suggestion, holds one meaning: selected or entered by the family. It is very legible and exact. Against it: Status's bright green bars are the loudest thing on that page, 'off' is only a tiny red square beside them, and on a phone Send sits alone on its own row.

It has the best typesetting and the fastest pages to scan. Every list is a one-line row read along a dotted leader to a tabular facts column, on slate bands with a head column, and the rule holds on Home, Ideas, To do, Status and Settings alike. The tuning scale under the bar is a nice period touch. It has little of the ring and track line art the owner prizes, heads wrap in the 10rem column, and the cost section on Status falls below the fold.

This is Signal Galley refined. Legends are set into the rails between end dashes, steel reverse video marks 'here', the case is thinner, and the To do boxes are square, so they read clearly as checkboxes. It is calm and usable and keeps the Coming up line and a Chat time track. The steel is so quiet that the page reads more monochrome than its parent, and it keeps only part of the line language.

Grounded green-black slate, the fortnight line with its breathing 'now' lamp, and a To do timetable margin. It is the solid base the top entrants were bred from. It dropped most of the line art the owner misses, and it keeps the heavy pewter case.

Its text-mode grammar (square windows, legends in the frame, reverse video) highlights the CRT motif well, and it has zero small targets. The pale steel reverse block is loud, double frames sit on every window, Status is barely green, and it has no tracks or rings.

The strips are well shaped, in the vein of the Galley Coming up rows the owner admired, and the targets are good. There is more periwinkle-blue than necessary, the case is the thick pewter slab, and there is almost no line art.
The column of ways to start is tidy. But the full-width Next up case makes the pewter slab the owner called too dominant even bigger, and every page below Home is the parent's.

The full-bleed bands delimit areas clearly, and the key-style buttons have obvious affordance. But the teal-graphite wash over the whole page makes one blue-green family with the phosphor, the band rules in five colours edge toward confetti, there is no line art, and 41 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

A calm, beautifully typeset atlas column, and the section discs in the bar are a nice wayfinding idea. But the serif pulls it off the CRT, it drops the lit glass greeting, the narrow single column wastes desktop width (Home is 2942px long), and 45 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.
Reverse Video's grammar is good, but it is cut from oxblood-brown Bakelite. The owner said brown and warm colours do not match the phosphor, and red beside green reads as seasonal.
Wine Bakelite and old-rose labels are the pink and warm tones the owner has rejected. The hanging heads leave switched-off margin, and 43 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.
The same wine and rose as Magic Eye, now with Fraunces titles, a serif that has pulled off the CRT every time it has been tried. The targets are as small as its parent's.

fixes.suggestion: Keep every line. Swap the thick rounded pewter case for Flight Deck's thin, square, screwed faceplate: this is the owner's standing critique, and it is the one thing holding Signal Lines back. Nudge the periwinkle accent toward a lower-chroma cyan, about #8fbfdc, in line with the owner's CGA note and to show less blue. Home's To do sets its title over the track and leaves the timetable margin empty beside it: hang the title from the head ring in the margin column instead. To do page: take the Add fold out of the head bracket so the bracket holds only Show, Search and Filter and the head stays short on a phone. Add a `late` field in views.task_row so overdue lamps are amber on the To do page as well as on Home. Where a head has nothing to hold, drop the buffer stop, or end the line in a small tick, so it does not read as a pin.

Keep the thin screwed faceplates, the legend-in-break brackets and the one-meaning cyan. On Status, make 'on' and 'off' the same shape and size: a 3px left edge for both, sage or #6dff9c for on and red for off. The glance then reads both, and seven bright bars no longer shout. On a phone, put Send on the From row beside the mic. Set family names in bone with only a cyan initial or edge, and keep cyan with an underline for links, so a name never looks clickable. Raise the legends to .8rem at .06em tracking. Graft Signal Lines' fortnight line onto Coming up and its timetable track onto To do, and round the bracket's one turning corner, which is the element the owner singled out.

Keep the one-line rows with leaders and a facts column, the head column and the tuning scale: they are the most usable structure in the field. Add line art: let a thin line drop from each band's head icon down the head column and turn under the rows, so Signal Box's bracket frames each band. Widen the head column to about 11.5rem, or set heads a step smaller, so 'Finish setting up' and 'The kids' wishes' stay on one line. On Status, set Who answers and Keys side by side at 72rem or wider so the cost band starts above the fold. The OPEN tags on To do are amber: make them neutral, since amber means 'needs a look'.

Lift the steel one step (#b7cfdf links, a #7f97a8 block), or use Flight Deck's cyan, so the companion shows at a glance. Keep the square checkboxes, which are the clearest tick affordance in the field, but hang them on To do's vertical track as Signal Lines does.

Keep the full-bleed bands that delimit each part, and the key buttons (All plans, All 4). Move the ground off teal to a neutral green-black slate. Give every band one steel rule with a short lead in its section's colour, instead of a full coloured rule. Bring the targets to 44px. Put a track in the Coming up and To do bands so the bands carry the line language.

Keep the section discs in the bar and the star for 'you are here', which make good wayfinding, and keep the calm measure. Restore the lit glass greeting. Use Plex for the interface, keeping the serif, if anywhere, for page titles only. Go two columns at desktop width so Home is not 2942px long, and raise the targets to 44px.
If the wide Next up scope is kept, make its case the thin square faceplate, so the rehang does not magnify the slab the owner already dislikes.

judges.notes:
On usability, which the user has asked about: I weighed it inside the owner's lens this round, using what the harness records (targets under 44px per page, identical Tab order in every entrant) and what the shots show (scan speed, affordance, sight lines, controls on a phone). It separated the field clearly.
- The informed entrants and the slate carried ones hit 0-3 of 56 Home targets under 44px.
- Magic Eye and its mutant, Attract Mode and Porcelain Atlas stay at 41-45, about today's 45 of 57. This usability loss is part of why they rank low.
- The most scannable pages are Programme Guide's: one-line rows, leaders and an aligned facts column on every page.
- The clearest affordances are Flight Deck's boxed selection and Signal Legend's square checkboxes.
- Signal Lines' tracks help people find their way: they delimit areas and lead the eye, as the owner said. Its round tick lamps rely on a known convention (Reminders or Things) rather than an obvious checkbox.

No lens on this panel asks directly whether a person can do the family's everyday tasks quickly. I recommend adding a usability judge that scores each candidate on concrete tasks: find the next plan, tick off a to-do, send a message with 'who is asking' chosen, see at a glance what is broken on Status, and filter Ideas. It should score each task on desktop and phone, reading targets, contrast of the smallest text, focus visibility and how many eye jumps each task takes.

On taste, three entrants now each hold one piece of what the owner has asked for:
- Signal Lines: the line language on every page.
- Flight Deck: the thin, square, detailed case, and cyan.
- Programme Guide: typesetting and scannability.

The natural next breed is Signal Lines' lines on Flight Deck's faceplates and colour code, with Programme Guide's one-line rows for Status and Settings. The palette measures agree with the picture: the winners sit at 64-75% green share with low neon in the other colour, so they are clearly less monochrome than today (83%) and still green-led.

scores.why: Every part of the soul the owner likes is here: the lit glass greeting pool, real tubes and glow in layers. But the whole page glows, so it keeps the Matrix glare and the monochrome, and nothing below the fold is grounded. This is the yardstick, the same as round 8's 4.0.

A TV listing lit by one green tube. It keeps the lit glass greeting with its cobalt corner, has the best answer yet to the case critique (a thinner, squarer case with a groove, vents and an LED, and scanlines on the glass), and adds a tuning scale whose needle stands under the page you are on. Below the fold, every list becomes a calm programme row on slate with dotted leaders and a tabular facts column. Glow stays scarce and means something, and the change shows on Home, Chat, Ideas (nine rows above the fold), Status and the month.

The consensus breed, done faithfully. The glass pool stays, as do the breathing now lamp on the fortnight line and the chinned tube, now thinner. Legends knocked into the rails and a quiet steel reverse video for 'here' give the page a text-mode panel grammar with no added green. It loses a little for staying close to its parent above the fold, and for Chat's long time track.

Still an excellent keeper of the soul: the lit greeting, the now lamp as the one live light below the fold, and grounded slate trays. But its child Signal Legend now does all of this and more, and the thick rounded pewter slab and the near-copy Status are unchanged.

The most CRT personality carried by grammar alone: frame legends, dialogs, and reverse video for 'this one'. The typed-in field still has no bloom, and the steel mass leaves Status the least lit page in the field.

A real period kin to the CRT: EFIS cockpit displays were 1980s tubes. The colour code gives every hue one meaning (green active, cyan entered by the family, amber caution), and the screwed faceplates with scanlines are lovely. But seven full-brand bars on Status spread the glow, the flush faceplate loses most of the home-monitor chin, and the cyan comes close to a stock link blue.

Signal Galley's soul is intact above the fold. The mimic-panel lines are drawn with a fine pen, but rings and tracks on every page, including Chat's message track and rings on To do, drift back toward the git-graph reading that round 7 retired.
Chinned tubes, scarce glow and an orderly rack of strips. It is calm and grounded, but the strips form a grey mass with little light in them: a well-kept console more than a lit tube.

Hanging the plot as a wide tube is a bold idea, and the greeting keeps its pool. But a 5:1 tube is not a real 1980s screen (they were 4:3), so it reads as a departures board. It also makes the pewter slab bigger and leaves the greeting's upper right as empty dark glass.

Better for the soul than Magic Eye, because the greeting pool and the chinned tubes come back and reverse video carries the period. But oxblood windows on Status, Chat and the month read red-and-green seasonal. The brown cases make the tubes look like a 1970s TV cabinet rather than a 1980s green screen.

An arcade after hours is real kin, and the roll bar that sweeps the tube at power-on is the best CRT behaviour in the round. But the graphite-teal ground makes one blue-green family with the phosphor, glow is at half of today's, the greeting's pool is weak and the select's focus ring has lost its halo. Squinted, the page reads as a teal wash, not a lit screen.

Calm and handsomely set, and the airglow rising off the horizon under the tube is lovely light. But Newsreader everywhere, a starfield, a greeting with no glass, a cobalt plastic case and uppercase flat buttons turn the page into a book about the night sky. The phosphor is a guest in it.
The magic-eye story still costs the soul most: there is no lit glass greeting, lit brightness is the lowest in the field, and green tubes in oxblood cases on wine plates read as seasonal.

Fraunces titles pull the parent further off the CRT, and the text dims one more step. Fields are still underline-only, so focus loses its green ring, which is part of the light. The greeting pool is still missing.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the tuning scale with its needle under the current place, the grooved thin case with vents, LED and scanlines, the one-line programme rows with dotted leaders and a right-hand facts column, the head column inside slate bands, and Chat as a log with names and times in a column. FIX: (1) Give the listing one live light below the fold. Graft Signal Galley's breathing #6dff9c now lamp into the date designator of Coming up's next event; this is the only thing Signal Legend has that this page lacks. (2) Stop the heads wrapping ('Finish setting up', 'The kids' wishes', 'What it has cost'). Use a head column of about 11.5rem, or step the band heads to about 1.3rem with text-wrap:balance. (3) Status: bring the spend tube above the fold. Tighten the band padding, or hang the cost band first, since it holds the page's only tube. (4) Keep VT323 on the machine's glass (the greeting date, FROM) but set form field labels in Plex Mono 500 at .78rem with .05em tracking, because VT323 under about 1.1rem blurs. (5) The 'Outing' kind label is a sage close to the brand. Move it toward a celadon of lower chroma, or tint the designator only. (6) Phone: put each band's head, icon and link on one line above the rows, to cut about a screen from Home.

KEEP: the rail legends, the steel reverse video, square family surfaces against round glass, and the fortnight line with its now lamp. FIX: (1) The thin case needs its groove to show at 1x: a 1px inset highlight (#ffffff14) over a 1px dark line (#0006), with the chin vents and LED kept. (2) Chat: drop the long vertical track. Keep the steel stops, and set each family message's time in its bubble header, so the time is not far from a right-hand bubble. (3) To do stamps: set 'was due · 2 days ago' on one line in an 8.5rem margin. (4) Drop the full stop from the count legend. (5) Plans' Coming up and Recently icons need their lead colour.

If it is carried again, give the typed-in field back its bloom (the green ring plus a soft 12px halo), use a single frame except on real dialogs, and take Signal Legend's quieter #748a9b reverse block. Otherwise let Signal Legend inherit it and retire it.

KEEP: the EFIS colour code (green means active, cyan means entered by the family, amber means caution), the demarcation lines with legends in the breaks and brackets that stay open on the right, and the screwed faceplates with scanlines. FIX: (1) On Status, make the on state a small #6dff9c lamp, or a 2px sage bar, not seven full-brand bars. (2) Give Next up, the 404 and Sign in a real chin under the faceplate (about 10px of lower bezel with vents and the LED), so the unit reads as a CRT and not a flat panel. (3) Pull the cyan down to about C .06-.07 (near #8fb6d2), so it reads as an instrument colour, not a link blue. (4) Set the legends at .8rem, weight 500, .05em tracking. (5) Balance Home's two columns.

KEEP: the roll bar that sweeps the tube at power-on (a true CRT behaviour, brief and one-shot), the full-width bands ruled in each section's colour, and keys with a little travel. FIX: move the ground and companion off teal (h169-194) to a neutral graphite near h240 with C about .010. Restore the lit glass greeting pool and the halo on focused selects. Give the current tab a raised lit cap rather than a sunken well, so it cannot read as disabled.

KEEP: the airglow rising off the horizon rule under the greeting's tube, the magnitude marks in the bar (a disc for each part, a star for the page you are on), and the rules tinted in each part's colour. FIX: bring back Plex or DM Sans for everything read, with a serif on h1 at most. Set the question back in its glass box with the green pool. Use the pewter chinned case, not cobalt plastic. Drop the starfield dots and the uppercase flat buttons.
The idea of reading the plot first is good, but the tube must stay 4:3. Hang a chinned 4:3 scope beside a departures list set as slate rows. Do not stretch the tube to 5:1.

Reverse Video's grammar reads better on steel. If Bakelite is kept, keep it only in the monitor case (one material with a job) and put the windows back on slate, so the page stops reading red and green.

judges.notes:
Through the soul lens this round has a real contest at the top, and both leaders keep everything the owner likes: a lit glass greeting, 1980s tubes, and glow that is scarce and means something.

Programme Guide is the first entrant to build Magic Eye's listing structure without the wine, and it comes first here for three reasons:
- It changes the most page content: Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas with nine rows above the fold, Status and the one-screen month.
- It has the finest typesetting in nine rounds.
- It answers the case critique best (thin, grooved, vents, LED, scanlines).
Its one soul debt is that nothing is live below the fold. The fix is Signal Legend's now lamp.

Signal Legend is the consensus breed, done faithfully. It has the clearest meaning for the light (the now lamp) and a text-mode panel grammar. It is the safer standard, but it is closest to what the panel has already seen.

A breed worth trying next is Programme Guide's rows, head column, tuning needle and case, with Signal Legend's now lamp, rail legends and steel reverse video. From Flight Deck, take its demarcation brackets for grouping.

The round's new ideas:
- Flight Deck's EFIS colour code is the best-argued system for what each colour means since round 1, and it deserves another round with a real chin and calmer Status lamps.
- Attract Mode's power-on roll bar is the best tube behaviour anyone has drawn.
- Porcelain Atlas's airglow is lovely light, in the wrong book.

The random entrants and the Magic Eye line keep failing the soul in the same two places: the greeting loses its glass pool, and the companion (teal, wine, oxblood, serif) pulls the page off the screen.

On the user's question about usability: round 8's panel had an interaction lens (targets, sight lines, keyboard and mouse, focus, Tab order), so usability has been judged. If this round's panel has no such lens, it should get one. Through the soul lens I marked down usability losses that are also losses of light:
- Magic Eye and Retitled have underline-only fields and focus with no green ring.
- Attract Mode's select focus has lost its halo, and its sunken current tab can read as disabled.
- Porcelain Atlas uses uppercase tracked buttons and small serif labels.
- Programme Guide's small VT323 field labels are hard to read.

Scale: the best entrant is now 4.6 points above today (8.6 against 4.0), against 4.4 in round 8.

scores.why: A stock dark-mode card grid washed in one green. It has a mood (the glowing tube) but no second voice, no type system beyond one sans, and nothing below the fold that anyone would remember. It is the 'Matrix' page the family named.

The first slate entrant with a real typographic identity. Condensed Instrument Sans heads sit in a head column like a TV listing, one-line rows run on dotted leaders to a right-aligned tabular column, kinds are named in their own colour at the row's end, and a tuning-scale ruler runs under the bar with a denim needle. It changes Home below the fold, Status (now a timetable), Chat (a name and time gutter), Ideas and Settings in one grammar: a system, calm and 'oh, that's lovely'. It loses points for heads that wrap in the 10rem column and for orphaned notes in the To do head column.

An inspired reframe: a 1982 glass cockpit was a CRT, so the EFIS code gives every colour one job (cyan for what the family entered or selected, bone for data, amber for caution, green for on). The fine demarcation brackets with the legend set in the break, and the label-over-data rows (THURSDAY 1 OCTOBER, 10:00 over the title), are elegant typesetting. It loses points because Status's seven full-height green bars are the loudest thing on the page, the cyan leans toward a stock link blue, and Chat barely changes.

Still a strong grammar: steel windows with their names knocked into the frame, reverse video for 'here', and unboxed rows. It reads as a calm old program on a modern screen. The reverse block is still pale and loud, the spaced mono-caps legends shout, and its cousins this round (Flight Deck, Bakelite Video) now do the same idea with more colour logic.

The mimic-panel line language is new and runs through every page: rings, tracks, hollow stops, and To do's overdue rings in amber on a track. It gives Chat, To do and Status a drawn structure that none of the others have. But ringing every section icon reads as a generic 'icon in a circle', the chunky pewter case stays, and above the fold it is still Signal Galley.

A tasteful, coherent refinement: legends set in double-hairline rails, a quiet steel reverse video for 'this one', and Chat's time track with stops. It is well made but incremental. The steel companion is so low in chroma that the page reads greyer and more monochrome than its parent, with little new mood.

The fortnight line with its one breathing now lamp is still one of the most memorable single moves in the tournament, and the slate trays are grounded. Status, Settings and Plans remain generic boxed grids, so the identity lives mostly on Home.

The boldest and most literary identity on the panel: a star atlas set as a book, with a Newsreader column, star-colour discs in the bar, an eight-rayed star for the current page, cobalt porcelain plates and a green airglow on the horizon rule. In isolation it is lovely and typeset with care. As Phosphor it falls short: the serif everywhere pulls it off the CRT, the monitors look pasted into a novel, the lit glass greeting pool is gone, a 45rem column leaves most of a desktop empty, and Status becomes a narrow stack of plates.

The most material mood on the panel: oxblood Bakelite windows, porcelain type and one green eye, in a radio at night. The oxblood fills every window, the ask box included, so the page squints red-brown and heavy, and the greige reverse-video tabs look like disabled tan buttons. Keep the idea of a material; use less of it.

Full-width graphite bands, each ruled in its section's colour, stratify the whole page. It is a real structural idea, and it carries colour into Home, Status and Ideas. But the teal ambient sits next to the green family and the page squints teal-grey, and Figtree with pill 'All plans →' keys reads as a stock SaaS dashboard rather than a machine.

Hanging Next up as a wide departures scope across the room is a brave structural move and the most memorable thing about it. It makes the grey pewter slab bigger, leaves empty glass, and everything past Home is the parent unchanged.
Tidy flight-strip racks on slate with a cobalt light, but it is the predictable periwinkle-and-slate identity and has the least personality of the carried four.

The programme-guide rows and one-screen month are good ideas (Programme Guide inherited them well). The wine and rose beside green still read as Christmas and alarm, and the hanging heads leave dead black margin down the left.

Soft Fraunces titles give it some magazine charm, but they are the serif that has faded in four rolls. It is the same wine Bakelite underneath, and the wider titles now wrap in the margin ('Finish / setting up'). A small change in the wrong direction.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the condensed display heads, the dotted leaders to a tabular facts column, the kind named in its colour at the row's end, the tuning-scale ruler with its needle, and the gutter in Chat. Fix these: (1) Heads wrap in the 10rem head column ('Finish / setting up', 'The kids' / wishes', 'What it / has cost'). Widen the column to about 11.5rem or set h2 at 1.3rem with -0.005em tracking so every head sits on one line. (2) The third setup step is lit amber with a steel edge, as if hovered or selected. Keep every step the same and mark only the next one, with the green 'next' lamp. (3) To do's head column holds '4 shown' and the time-zone note as a sidenote. Move the note under the filter and keep the head column for the title and its one action. (4) Swap the VT323 field labels for Plex Mono 500 at .72rem with .04em tracking: the pixel face reads as period costume at label size and hurts legibility. (5) On Status, move What it has cost above the fold. For example, put the cost tube in the head column of the first band, or put the cost band first. (6) Shade the month's weekend columns and today with the denim needle. The month is still a field of uniform cells. (7) On the phone, cut the band padding and let the head sit inline with its count, so Home is not three screens long.

Keep the EFIS colour code (each colour one meaning), the demarcation brackets with the legend set in the break and links at the right end, the label-over-data rows, and the square screwed faceplates for the machine. Fix these: (1) Replace Status's full-height #6dff9c bars with a 6px lamp and a 2px sage edge, so bright green is a light, not a stripe. (2) Move the cyan from #83bfec toward a steel-cyan (#9cc3da) so it stops reading as a Tokyo Night or One Dark link blue. (3) Something to eat should be a neutral plate with only its icon in amber. Amber must mean only caution, and today the restaurant colour muddies it. (4) Give Chat the cockpit grammar too. Vera's lines could sit on a display-unit faceplate and the family's on matte plates with the cyan edge, with times in a legend column, so Chat is visibly different from today. (5) Draw the screws at 9-10px, or drop them. At 7px they read as notched corners.

The idea worth keeping is the atlas's sign system: a disc in each part's star colour, a smaller disc for each kind, a star for 'you are here', and the green airglow rising off a horizon rule. So is its care for measure and leading. Fix these to make it Phosphor: (1) Restore the lit glass greeting. Put the ask box in the green-black glass pool with the airglow behind it, not on bare night. (2) Use Newsreader only for h1 and h2 and for Vera's lines, and set rows, controls, Status and facts in Instrument Sans and Plex Mono, so the serif is a voice, not the whole page. (3) At 72rem or more, set the column as a two-page spread of facing plates (Coming up | To do; Lately added | Wishes) rather than one 45rem strip, so the desktop is not three-quarters empty. (4) Keep an icon beside each disc in the bar and give the tab bar its icons back. Dots alone lose recognition and the targets fall under 44px. (5) Make Status a star-chart table, one-line rows with leaders, not a narrow stack of plates.

Take the reverse block to #6e8496-#7a93a6 and the legends to Plex Mono 500 at .72rem with .05em tracking. Put a single frame on windows and a double one only on dialogs. Link text set in frame lines needs an arrow or underline so it does not read as a label. Fold the frame into one --frame token to buy CSS room.

Keep the tracks, the hollow stops, and To do's overdue rings on a track. They are the best part and carry structure into Chat and Status. Drop the ring around every section icon, which reads as a generic icon badge, and let the track start at a plain tick. Fill To do's empty timetable margin beside the head. Replace the chunky pewter case with a thin, square, flush case.

Keep the Bakelite as a frame and chrome material (bar, window frame lines, monitor case) but put the window fills back on a near-neutral dark (oxblood at 30-40% of today's chroma), and keep the ask box in green-black glass. Swap the greige reverse block for a warm porcelain on the bar only, or for steel. The whole page squints maroon today.

Keep the full-width bands ruled in each section's colour, and the kind edges on the cards. They carry colour into every page. Move the ambient off teal h194 to a blue-graphite or warm graphite so the companion leaves the green family. Replace the pill 'All plans →' keys with plain links set on the rule. Make the latched tab a lit cap rather than a sunk well, so it does not read as disabled.

The wide departures scope is worth keeping. Make its case thin and flush (Radar Room's direction), and fill the spare glass with the next two or three departures on dotted leaders, so it earns its width.

judges.notes: Through my lens, the best has moved from 3 (today) to 8. Programme Guide is the first slate entrant whose identity comes from typesetting rather than paint. Its condensed heads, dotted leaders, tabular facts and coloured kind names change every page, which is exactly what the owner's 'reflect more of the page content' asks for, and the owner enjoys typesetting. Flight Deck is the most inspired companion logic: a 1982 glass cockpit really was a CRT, and its EFIS code gives each colour one job. A breed of the two is the obvious next step: Programme Guide's listing rows and type steps inside Flight Deck's demarcation brackets and colour code. The random entrants reached further than the bred ones again. Porcelain Atlas is the most memorable page on the panel but stops being Phosphor. Attract Mode's banding carries colour across the page but reads SaaS-teal. Both have parts worth grafting (Atlas's discs, magnitude marks and horizon airglow; Attract Mode's section-coloured band rules). The wine and oxblood family (Magic Eye, Retitled, Bakelite Video) keeps a real mood, but over whole windows it keeps squinting red. On usability, which the user's relayed message says may not be judged anywhere: style and use overlap here, and the panel should weigh it explicitly, probably with a dedicated usability judge, as the user suggests. From what I saw: Programme Guide's one-line rows and Flight Deck's label-over-data rows scan fastest, since each row reads left to right to one tabular answer. Porcelain Atlas drops the bar icons, uses tiny spaced caps and has 45/56 Home targets under 44px. Magic Eye and Retitled have 43/56 and Attract Mode 41/56. Hanging-head layouts (Magic Eye, Retitled, Programme Guide's head column) push a list's first row right and down. Attract Mode's sunk 'latched' tab can read as disabled. Reverse Video's links set in frame lines read as labels. A usability judge should check sight lines, target sizes, Tab order through the moved controls (frame-line tabs, head-column links), how fast a row gives up its answer, and whether 'here' reads as chosen and not as disabled.

scores.why: Yardstick. Today's rounded cards and pills are consistent, but there is no type scale, facts column or list component, green is nearly everywhere, and 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px.

Still a complete system: masthead, Oxford rails, slate trays, one strip, timetable margin and the fortnight line, with 0 small targets and clear periwinkle links. Status and Settings are Galley copies, Chat splits times into two gutters, and its best ideas have now been bred forward into Signal Legend and Programme Guide.

The window, legend and reverse-video grammar holds on every page and passes all target checks. But links set in the bottom frame line ('All plans →', 'All 4 →') read as captions, not as things to click, and the tracked mono-caps legends still shout.

Tidy flight-strip racks with kind-tinted designators and few small targets (3 of 56). The board under the racks can't be seen, Status is racks on black, and apart from colour it adds nothing to the system that Galley doesn't already have.

A coherent programme-guide idea, but it fails as a working system. Fields are underlines, bracket buttons are a gimmick, 43 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, the hanging heads leave empty margin, and wine plates beside the red off lamps blur the one colour that means a fault.

The most finished version of the slate system. Legends and links sit in the rails, with underlined steel links that clearly read as links. Steel reverse video marks 'here' in the bar, tabs, menu and today on the month, so amber keeps its one job. Family surfaces are square, machine glass is round, and it holds on Status, Plans and To do. Costs: Chat's family times sit in a far-left gutter away from their bubbles, and Send drops to its own line on desktop.

The best system for use at a glance. Every part is a band with a head column, and every list (Coming up, To do, Ideas, Status, Settings) is one row read across a dotted leader to a facts column. That gives nine idea rows above the fold, Status as three short tables, Settings as one scannable list, and 0 small targets. Faults: the head links are grey spaced mono caps that read as labels, the facts sub-columns are ragged rather than tabular, heads wrap in the 10rem column, and the VT323 field labels are harder to read.

Label-over-data and a strict colour code (cyan for selected or entered, sage for on, amber for caution) are a real system principle, and Home and Plans are very legible. Usability slips: 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought' are drawn as legends in a line, so they lose their button affordance. Setup steps are drawn as empty checkboxes. The 'OPEN' tag is in caution amber. Family names share the link cyan.

One consistent line language, but it adds delimiters without adding information. Rings sit on every head and buffer stops read as pins, and the To do head's bracket holds a whole form (about 500px on a phone before the list). The Chat track is the one place the lines earn their weight.

Magic Eye's usability faults remain: underline fields, a select with no ring, bracket keys, 43 of 56 small targets. The Fraunces titles wrap in the margin ('Finish / setting up', 'What it / has cost'). The ruled line from each title to its action is the one good addition.

The departures-board scope is a fair idea, but the full-width pewter slab is mostly empty glass. The ways to start move into a side column that empties when someone types, and Home grows 170px. Below Home it is Plotting Room unchanged.

Reverse Video's grammar carries over cleanly, with 0 small targets. But the oxblood plates put the red off rings and the amber setup on a red-brown ground, so warnings stand out less, and the greige 'here' block reads close to disabled.

The clearest affordance language in the field: keys with travel you press, sunk wells you type in, bands with ruled caps. Home bands read well. But the keys are about 36px (41 of 56 under 44), the select focus is a faint sage edge, not the ring, and the current tab latched down reads as disabled. The lifted teal-graphite ground makes it a generic dashboard, while Ideas, To do and Status stay boxed cards much like today.

Beautifully typeset, and a coherent atlas system that would hold on Settings and Status. As a tool it costs a lot: one 45rem column leaves half the desktop empty, Home runs to 2942px, 'ALL 4' and 'ADD AN IDEA' are grey tracked caps that don't read as links, 14 Home targets are under 24px, the focus ring is 1px, and the phone tab bar loses its icons.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the band, head column, one-line row, dotted leader and facts column. It is the best list standard yet, so apply it to Wishes, Memory and idea detail too. (1) Make head links look like links: sentence-case Instrument Sans .9rem in denim with a 1px underline ('All plans →'), not spaced mono caps. (2) Make the facts truly tabular: give each row fixed sub-columns, e.g. grid-template-columns: 3.25rem minmax(0,1fr) 24ch 13ch 9ch, so distance, 'for …' and kind line up down Ideas and Status instead of drifting with the leader. (3) Stop heads wrapping: 11.5rem head column or 1.3rem heads; below about 72rem, set the head above its rows. (4) Replace the VT323 field labels with Plex Mono 500 .72rem caps at .05em. (5) Take 'OPEN' off amber (slate tag) so amber stays 'needs a look'. (6) Move To do's note out of the 20ch head column into the lede. (7) In Chat, right-align the family speaker's name and time beside their bubble.

Keep the legends in the rails, the steel reverse video for 'here', the square/round split, the underlined steel links and today as a steel block. (1) Put Send on the From row on desktop (as Programme Guide and Attract Mode do); it now takes a line of its own. (2) In Chat, put each family message's time at the bubble's outer edge, not in the far-left gutter. (3) Thin the double-rule rails to one hairline plus a short 2px lead, so eight rails on Home don't read as ruled paper. (4) Borrow Programme Guide's one-line rows for Status and the Settings overview; they are still Galley's tiles.
It has been superseded by its child, Signal Legend. If it stays, give it Legend's underlined links and reverse video, and Programme Guide's one-line rows on Status.

Keep label-over-data (mono label line above a sans title), the colour-meaning code and the demarcation legends for read-only sections. Things you act on must keep their affordance. (1) 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought for later' go back to a bounded box with + and a sans label; a legend in a line says 'section', not 'button'. (2) Setup steps get the amber ring or an arrow, not an empty checkbox that invites a tick. (3) Give family names bone or grey-blue so cyan means 'link or selected' only, and underline every link. (4) Put the Status on bars on sage (#86d9a6) and keep the brand for live lamps. (5) Put 'Due …' on one line (nowrap).

Keep the affordance grammar and breed it into the slate system: raised keys = press, sunk wells = type in, latched = here. It is the clearest usability idea this round. (1) Put it on green-black slate (ground #0b0e0d, bands #0f1519); the lifted teal-graphite greys the black and makes one blue-green family. (2) Make keys min-height 2.75rem to clear 44px targets. (3) Give select, checkbox and key :focus-visible the 2px #6dff9c outline with 2px offset; the select's faint sage edge fails. (4) Show the current tab as a tinted raised solid with a 2px steel cap, not sunk and lower, which reads disabled. (5) Carry the bands onto Ideas, To do and Status as rows, not cards.

Keep the rule tinted by its own section's colour, the magnitude marks and the typographic care. To make it a tool: (1) Use a two-column desk at 72rem or more (reading column plus a facts or aside column), so Home is not 2942px and half the screen empty. (2) Links in sentence case, underlined, in the cobalt accent, not grey tracked caps. (3) 44px targets and a 2px #6dff9c focus outline. (4) Put icons back on the phone tab bar. (5) If a serif stays, keep it to h1 and h2; a serif in chat bubbles and list titles slows scanning.

Keep the Chat track with stops, where the line carries order. Drop the rings on every head, the buffer stops and the bracket around To do's form. The line language should mark only time or sequence (Coming up, Chat, To do's due column).

judges.notes:
The owner's usability question: I weighed usability inside this lens, and it separated the field more than colour did. The slate informed entrants and Reverse Video/Bakelite have 0 Home targets under 44px. The random and Magic Eye lines do not: Attract Mode 41/56, Porcelain Atlas 45/56 with 14 under 24px, Magic Eye and its mutant 43/56. The usability faults found, by kind:
(a) Links that read as labels: Programme Guide's spaced mono caps, Reverse Video and Bakelite's bottom-frame links, Porcelain's grey caps.
(b) Actions drawn as section legends: Flight Deck's 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought'.
(c) Links drawn as tickable checkboxes: Flight Deck's and Magic Eye's setup steps.
(d) Fields as underlines with no focus ring: Magic Eye and Retitled.
(e) Weak focus: Attract Mode's select, Porcelain's 1px ring.
(f) 'Here' that reads as disabled: Attract Mode's latched tab, Bakelite's greige block.
(g) Length: Porcelain 2942px, Plotting Room Rehung +170px.
(h) Sight lines: a family message's time far from its bubble (Signal Legend; Programme Guide on desktop).

A dedicated usability judge would be worth adding. Much of this is checkable and could be scored as a measure rather than left to taste:
- targetsUnder44 per page (already in health.json);
- links carrying a non-colour cue (underline or arrow) and differing from nearby labels by at least 3:1;
- every :focus-visible showing an outline of 2px or more at 3:1;
- disclosures and buttons drawn as bounded boxes;
- page height per page;
- a Tab-order walk past stop 18.
Task-based checks from screenshots would add to those: find what's next, tick a task, add an idea, change a setting, reach Send with the thumb on a phone.

Top of the field: Programme Guide gives the family the fastest read of any entrant (one row, one leader, one facts column on every page). Signal Legend is the most finished frame. The breed to try is Legend's rails, reverse video and underlined links holding Guide's one-line rows and head column, with Attract Mode's raised/sunk/latched control grammar on slate for everything you press or type in.

scores.why: Every section is a card, and Ideas and To do each have two green primaries (Add and Filter), so the eye has no single action. 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px, Home runs 2111px, and the Month grid and Status's cost both sit below the fold.

Each head carries its link on the same line, the fortnight line reads at a glance, To do puts the late items first in its timetable margin, and Filter drops to secondary, leaving one green action per page. Almost no small targets (Plans 3, Settings 1). It loses points for the ring-shaped tick wells, which read as radio buttons, for splitting Chat's times into two gutters, and for Status's cost falling below the fold.

Reverse video makes 'where am I' the clearest on the panel, in the bar, the tabs and the phone cell alike, with zero small targets on any page. Home is dense and short (1675px), and the Month grid and Status's cost fit on screen. It loses points because 'All plans' and 'All 4' sit at each window's bottom right, away from their heads, and the tabs knocked into the frame line read as labels, not controls.

Heads with their links on one line and scannable strips with a facts column make this a clean, predictable page. A periwinkle underline marks the current page and tab, which is only moderately visible when squinting. Designators leave 2 to 9 targets under 24px on most pages, and Home is 1742px.

One-line programme rows make Home the shortest on the panel (1578px) and very quick to scan, and the Month grid fits. But the Ideas and Plans tabs sit in the far-left margin, away from the content they switch, and the bracketed [ Send ] and [ Filter ] read as text rather than buttons. The current page is a thin needle, and 43 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

Its steel reverse block for 'here' (bar, tabs, Settings nav, today on the month) is the one state marker that survives the squint strip. Every head's link sits in its rail, square tick wells look tickable, Status's cost is above the fold, and no page has a target under 44px. What holds it back: Chat's left time gutter parts the family's times from their right-hand bubbles, the phone's current cell is too faint, and To do's stamps stack in two parts.

The quickest page on the panel for finding things. Each band has its head column, and one-line rows run across dotted leaders to a facts column. All of Home is in 1646px, nine ideas show above the fold, Status and Settings read as one-line ledgers, the Month grid fits, and no target is under 44px. What holds it back: the 'here' needle vanishes when squinting, some rows are long for the eye to cross at 1280, the condensed heads wrap in the 10rem column, and the VT323 field labels are harder to read.

Clear affordances: Send sits at the end of the From row, List and Month move into the Plans head beside the title, links are underlined cyan, the 'here' box is outlined, and no target is under 44px. Comprehension loses a little. The .76rem mono legends make section heads smaller than their row titles, and the label-over-data rows put 'ALEX' before the task. Setup's square marks look tickable but are not, and 'Add something to do' set as a legend in the rule reads as a label, not a button.

Its bracket is the best head idea on the panel: title, tabs, 'Save a thought' and 'Add an idea' sit in one row, and To do's Add, Show and Search share one line, so every list starts sooner. But the bar marks the current page with a tiny dot, the weakest 'here' among the informed entrants. Tick wells are radio-like rings on a track, the track eats width on phone Chat, and Home is the longest of the informed (1967px).

Each head now runs title, rule, action along one line, which is a real sight-line gain. But the serif heads wrap in the 12rem margin ('Finish setting up', 'What it has cost'), the text is a step dimmer, and all the parent's interaction faults remain: margin tabs, bracketed buttons, and 43 of 56 Home targets under 44px.

The ways to start, set as keys beside the box, sit within reach of Send, and pairing Coming up with To do on one head line reads well. Moving Next up into a full-width scope makes 'what's next' unmissable, but it pushes the lists down (1914px), and ask.js hides the key column while someone types, so the layout shifts. Every other page is the parent's, with its sub-24px designators.

It keeps Reverse Video's grammar: a greige reverse block for 'here', zero small targets, Home at 1642px, and Status's cost on screen. To do rows are tighter, with the reminder and the edit fold on one line. The red off lamps are harder to tell apart on oxblood than on steel, and links still sit at the bottom right of each window instead of on its head.

The keys on the right of each band head ('All plans →') are the most obviously pressable links on the panel, and the bands separate cleanly. But the latched 'current' state reads backwards. On Ideas and Plans the chosen tab is the dark, sunk one, while the unchosen one looks raised and lit, so a newcomer would pick the wrong one. To do on Home reads in a Z across two columns, and 41 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

Each item is calm and readable, and spelling Memory, Family and Status out in the bar beats today's bare icons. But the single 45rem column makes Home 2942px and stacks Status into one long scroll. Head links ('ALL 4', 'ADD AN IDEA') are tiny tracked caps with no arrow or underline, buttons are small caps, the phone tabs lose their icons, and 45 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the bands, the one-line rows, the leaders and the facts column: they are the best finding structure on the panel. Make 'here' survive a squint by replacing the bar and phone needle with a filled denim cell and a 2px cap, or Signal Legend's reverse block, and the same on the head-column tabs. Cap row width (about 60rem, or pull the facts column in beside the detail) so a title and its fact sit within one saccade. At 1280, set heads at 1.3rem with nowrap or widen the head column to 11.5rem so 'Finish setting up' and 'The kids' wishes' stay on one line. Set head links in sentence case at .8rem with the arrow instead of spaced caps, and put field labels in Plex Sans 500 .8rem rather than VT323. On Status, trim band padding so the cost band starts above 900px. On phone Chat, keep the family's messages on the right.

Keep the reverse-video 'here', the links in the rails and the square tick wells. Use the same --rev block for the phone's current cell, since #1f2a31 is too faint to find. On Chat, hang each time beside its own bubble, on that bubble's side, or give the family a right-hand gutter, so no time sits 700px from its message. On To do, set the stamp on one line ('2 days ago' in amber under a small 'was due' tag) or widen the margin to 8.5rem. Keep Earlier and Later in the month rail, but give them the arrow keys' 44px box.

Move each window's 'All plans →' or 'All 4 →' from the bottom frame up to the right end of its title frame line, so the head and its action share a sight line, as Signal Legend does. Draw the frame-line tabs (ALL IDEAS | RESTAURANTS, LIST | MONTH) as real reverse-video buttons at full label size rather than as legends.

Keep Send inline, the view switch in the head row, the underlined cyan links and the outlined 'here' box: they are clear affordances. Section legends should outrank row titles: Plex Sans 600 at .95rem in sentence case, with mono kept for labels. Put the title first in each row and the ALEX or ACTIVITY label beside or under it, not above. Mark the setup steps with rings or arrows, not squares that look like checkboxes. Draw 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought for later' as bounded disclosure rows with a chevron, not as legends set in a rule. On Status, light 'on' as sage dots and keep #6dff9c for what is live.

The bracket that gathers a head's controls beside its title is worth making standard on every page: it shortens the path from title to action to content. Replace the tiny bar dot with a 2px cap and a tinted cell. Use square tick wells, since a ring on a track reads as a radio button or a stop. Hide the chat track below 40rem so phone bubbles get their width back. Give the stub heads (Status, Settings) no drop at all rather than a buffer stop.

Invert the latch. The current tab, Settings item and bar item should be the lit one (teal cap or filled key), and the others raised but dim. Sunk means 'field', and nothing else. Keep the band-head keys at the right ('All plans →'): they are the clearest links on the panel. Give keys and row links a 44px minimum height, and list To do on Home in one column so its time order reads top to bottom.

Carry forward the text-labelled bar (Memory, Family, Status, Settings named, not iconic), but in sentence case at .82rem with its icons kept on the phone tabs. Head links need an arrow, sentence case, at least .8rem and a 44px hit box. At 72rem and wider, let Home's lower sections and Status's three groups sit in columns inside the atlas margins, so Home is not 2942px long and the cost is not four screens down. Set buttons in sentence case with their icons.

Keep the ways to start as keys beside the box, but reserve their column while typing so nothing shifts. Halve the full-width Next up scope, or set it in the paired row with Coming up, so the lists start above the fold again.
Move the view tabs from the far-left margin into the head row beside the title, drop the [ ] brackets on buttons, and give every control a 44px minimum height. Keep the one-line programme rows.

judges.notes:
Through this lens the panel splits cleanly into two groups. The Signal family, Reverse Video, Bakelite Video, Flight Deck and Programme Guide have zero targets under 44px on every page (Signal Galley and Signal Lines still have 3 on Plans and 1 on Settings, Plotting Room and Rehung have 2 to 9 designators under 24px). The random seeds and the Magic Eye line are still at today's level (41 to 45 of 56 on Home). The Tab order on Home is identical in every candidate, since the DOM is unchanged, and every focus ring is the same bright #6dff9c, so keyboard use neither gained nor lost; moved controls (frame-line tabs, rail links, head brackets) keep their DOM position.

The biggest comprehension differences come from four things:
(1) Whether 'here' survives a squint. Reverse video (Signal Legend, Reverse Video, Bakelite Video) does; Flight Deck's outline and the pills mostly do; needles and dots (Programme Guide, Signal Lines, Magic Eye) do not; Attract Mode's latch reads backwards.
(2) Whether a head and its action share one line. Signal Legend's rails, Flight Deck's legend lines, Attract Mode's keys, Retitled's title rule and Signal Lines' bracket do; Reverse Video and Bakelite Video put the links at the bottom, and Magic Eye puts its tabs in a far margin.
(3) One green primary per page. Every informed entrant fixed today's second green Filter.
(4) Whether a control looks like what it does. Rings as tick wells read as radio buttons, Flight Deck's setup squares look tickable but are not, and disclosures set as legends read as labels.

Candidate principles for the standard:
(a) The current place is marked by a filled block or a cap that is visible when blurred, never only by colour or a dot.
(b) A section's action sits on its head's line, at the right.
(c) One #6dff9c primary per page.
(d) Tickable things are square wells; status marks are rings or lamps.
(e) Every control is at least 44px.
(f) Home's lower sections fit within about 1.8 screens at 1280.

On the owner's test, Programme Guide, Signal Legend, Flight Deck and Bakelite Video change the whole page, including Status, To do and Settings. Rehung changes little beyond Home, and Retitled changes little beyond its heads.

scores.why: DM Sans everywhere with mono only in the tubes: heavy tight-tracked titles, dates set proportional ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56'), no aligned facts column, and card grids with no typographic rhythm. It is legible, but it has no type system with steps.

A real system: the masthead (title and deck on one baseline over an Oxford rule), the Plex Mono facts and hung due stamps on To do, and tabular numerals on the fortnight day tiles. It pairs DM Sans heads with Plex Mono rather than one superfamily, its mono-caps counts ('4 SHOWN (UP TO 100).') are over-tracked, and Chat splits its times into two gutters.

Plex Sans with Plex Mono as one superfamily, legends knocked into the frame line, and right-aligned mono due times that read straight down. This is coherent, period-true typesetting on every page. The .78rem mono-caps legends still shout a little, and links set in spaced mono caps ('Change a key') read as labels.
Clean Plex strips with a tabular facts column and sentence-case heads with a leader to their link. It is orderly but typographically plain, and the 3-line To do strips waste vertical rhythm.

The condensed Instrument Sans display and the one-line programme-guide rows with right-aligned facts are fine typesetting. But the hanging heads leave a dead 12rem margin and wrap, the old-rose .74rem caps on wine are low in legibility, and 43 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

Moving to one Plex superfamily and setting each head on its rail is a good typesetter's device, and it changes Home, Status and Chat below the fold. Against it: Plex Sans Bold at 3rem is clunky, the double rails and the two voices of legend (sans heads, mono-caps counts ending in a period) are fussy, and Chat's time gutter sits far from the family's bubbles, which breaks the sight line.

The most complete type system in the round: condensed Instrument Sans for titles and heads, text width for body, Plex Mono for facts, seven steps, and every list a one-line row read across a dotted leader. Status and the Settings overview become leader rows you take in at a glance, and Chat gets a proper said-by gutter. The faults are the heads that wrap in the 10rem column, VT323 field labels, very long leaders on wide Status rows, and a To do page not yet rebuilt as rows.

An exact code: bone sans for data, grey Martian Mono condensed caps for labels, legends set in the breaks of a demarcation line, and label-over-data (the date above the title) with tabular facts on the right. It is disciplined and new. But disclosures such as 'Save a thought for later' become caps legends that read as labels rather than actions, To do mixes a legend ('SEARCH') and a label ('Show') in one form, Vera's bubble is narrow and leaves the orphan 'a backup.', and the caps label lines ('ALEX #4 · OPEN') get noisy.

Signal Galley's type is unchanged, and the ring-and-bracket line art adds structure but no typographic gain. The Ideas and To do mastheads now stack tabs, fold and filters inside the bracket, which crowds the title, and Home's To do head leaves its margin empty beside the title.

The Fraunces title line with its rule running to the page's one action is a handsome masthead. But the serif pulls off the CRT again, the section heads now wrap to two lines ('Finish / setting up', 'What it / has cost'), and the straight apostrophe in 'kids'' shows at display size. The parent's small-caps legibility problems remain.

Typographically the parent, with ink one step brighter; that is a small legibility gain, but brighter text works against the calm the owner asked for. The wide departures-board scope sets Next up on one line nicely, but it leaves slack glass inside the scope.

It keeps Reverse Video's Plex grammar, but its legends drop to .68rem mono caps ('WHO ANSWERS'), which is too small to read comfortably, and it sets the sentence 'No active reminder.' in mono. Warm porcelain ink on oxblood slightly lowers the contrast of small text.

Figtree with Martian Mono reads friendly but generic (SaaS), with no timetable or facts column and To do still in cards like today. Its full-width bands give pacing but little hierarchy, the band headings all share one weight and size, and 41 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

The most crafted book typesetting on show: a 45rem measure, generous leading, a Newsreader display greeting, tracked caps labels and mono date lines under titles. But serif body text in controls and in .8rem metadata is thin on dark, the all-caps nav and buttons (SEND, FILTER, ADD AN IDEA) lose word shapes, Home runs to 2942px, and it drops the glass greeting. The register fights Phosphor.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the condensed/text-width pairing, the leader rows and the said-by gutter: they are the best typesetting yet. Fix: (1) Stop the heads wrapping. Widen the head column to 11.5-12rem, or set the heads at 1.3rem condensed with text-wrap:balance, so 'Finish setting up', 'The kids’ wishes' and 'What it has cost' hold one line; below about 72rem, stack each head above its rows. (2) Replace the VT323 field labels with Plex Mono 500 at .72rem and .04em tracking; VT323 at 1.08rem is fuzzy and a fourth voice. (3) Put the facts in a fixed right column about 16-18rem wide, set in Plex Mono or with tabular-nums, so times like '10:00' and '19:00' align, and cap Status rows so the leader never runs about 900px. (4) Set links in sentence case with an arrow ('Change a key →'), not spaced mono caps that read as labels. (5) On Ideas, drop the kind word at the far right, since the tinted designator already says it, or move it beside the title, so the facts read distance, then who, then #. (6) Rebuild To do as the same one-line rows as Home: due hung left, 'No active reminder.' in the facts, not on a line of its own.

Keep the EFIS code (grey mono labels, bone data), the legends set in the break of the demarcation line, and label-over-data on Coming up. Fix: (1) Anything you press is not a legend. Put 'Save a thought for later', 'Add something to do' and 'Exact position and travel times' back into sentence-case sans with their chevron, and keep caps legends for section names only. (2) Use one pattern per form: on To do, 'SEARCH' is a legend but 'Show' is a label; make both labels. (3) Widen Vera's bubble to about 60-62ch so her reply breaks in two lines, not three with the orphan 'a backup.'. (4) Trim each caps label line to two tokens ('ALEX · DUE 27 SEP'), and let the OPEN chip go, since open is the default. (5) Consider Plex Mono condensed, or Plex Mono, in place of Martian Mono, so the sans and mono are one superfamily.
Set the frame legends at 500 .76rem with .05em tracking, and give links set in the frame an arrow and sentence case so they read as links. Carry Flight Deck's tabular right facts onto Coming up.

Set the 3rem titles in Plex Sans 600 with -0.01em tracking, not Bold. Use a single rail under each head instead of the double rule. Drop the period from mono count legends ('4 SHOWN · UP TO 100'). Bring Chat's time stops into the gutter beside each bubble, family times on the right, so time and message sit on one sight line.

The atlas's measure, leading and quiet hierarchy are worth breeding, but keep Newsreader for h1, h2 and Vera's replies only. Set body text, controls, options and all metadata under 1rem in Instrument Sans or Plex Sans. Buttons and nav go back to sentence case at .875rem or more, with icons. Restore the glass greeting pool. Let lists and Status break the 45rem measure, as tables do in a book. Tighten list leading to about 1.35, and put 'No active reminder' in the date line, to bring Home from 2942px to under 2000px.

If Fraunces stays, use it for the page h1 only, at opsz 72+ and weight 300-350, and keep the section heads in the condensed sans so they do not wrap. Keep the title line with its rule running to the one action: it is a good masthead to graft onto Programme Guide.

judges.notes: What I looked at: the strip for each candidate, full-size Status, Ideas, To do and General shots, the Settings, Plans, phone Home and squint sheets, detail strips for Programme Guide and Flight Deck, and zoomed crops of timetables, heads and chat. A usability note first, since the owner asked whether it is judged. My lens covers legibility (size, case, contrast of small type, measure, orphans) and how scannable lists are, and I scored those in. It does not cover task success: finding the next plan, ticking a to-do, telling a disclosure from a label, target sizes, Tab order, or how much scrolling it takes to reach something. Several of this round's strongest typographic moves have exactly those costs, all scored in above: Flight Deck turns actions into caps legends; Porcelain Atlas sets its nav and buttons in small spaced caps and runs Home to 2942px; Programme Guide's heads wrap and its VT323 labels are fuzzy; Magic Eye, Retitled, Attract Mode and Porcelain Atlas each have 41-45 of 56 Home targets under 44px. I recommend adding a usability judge who scores task by task (find, act, return, keyboard, phone thumb reach), because no current lens owns that. On type overall: the best of the round has come a long way from today (8.1 against 4.5). The winning pattern is a condensed display width for heads, a text width for body and a mono facts column read across a leader. Programme Guide's leader rows on Status and the Settings overview are the most glanceable Status and Settings in nine rounds; breed them. Flight Deck's label-over-data and legends in the line break are the most original typographic grammar; they need restraint in how often mono caps appears. Porcelain Atlas proves the owner's taste for typesetting can be served by measure and leading without a serif body; graft its measure discipline for prose (ledes, help text, Vera's replies at 60-62ch), not its serif controls. One source-text fix every entrant shares: 'The kids' wishes' and 'The kids' conversations' use a straight apostrophe while 'What’s on your mind?' uses a curly one; make them ’ in the templates or views.py. It shows at display size in the serif and condensed heads.

But the All ideas / Restaurants and List / Month tabs are tiny caps knocked into frame lines and read as labels, so 'show only restaurants' is hard to find.

Every control looks like what it is: pill tabs sit over the list, checkboxes are square, overdue is amber on Home, and only 3 targets are small. Scanning is calm, but the month is still past the fold and Ideas shows about five rows.

But 43 of 56 Home targets are small, '[ Send ]' and '[ Filter ]' brackets read as text, fields are underline-weak (Sign in too), and the Ideas and Plans tabs sit far off in the left margin.

Checkboxes are square with amber overdue, weekends are shaded and 0 targets are small. It loses points because the month is still past the fold, Earlier/Later became small text links in the rail, and Chat's time gutter sits far from the family's right-hand bubbles.

The most usable at a glance. Home answers 'what's on', 'what's overdue' and 'what's new' in about 1.4 screens of one-line rows with dotted leaders. Amber 'OPEN' on every task dilutes caution, and the setup links have square boxes that invite a tick.

The heads are efficient: Ideas' tabs, Save and Add share one head, and To do's Add and filter sit above the list. But the to-do checkboxes are rings on a track, the same rings used as decoration on the Chat track, so a newcomer cannot tell which circles are pressable. The To do page shows no overdue flag, and the month is past the fold.

Magic Eye's at-a-glance layout, with text a step dimmer (ink 13.3) and serif heads that wrap to two lines in the margin. The small targets (43/56), the bracket buttons, the underline fields and the far-off margin tabs are all unchanged, and the title at x=32 against the lede at x=260 breaks the sight line.

Home now reads in task order: the ask with Send on its row, the ways to start as keys beside it, then Coming up beside To do (square boxes, amber overdue). The text is one step brighter (13.5), kind to tired eyes. The wide Next up band pushes the lists about 170px down, the month is past the fold, and 3 targets are small.

Reverse Video's clear 'here' block in greige, 0 small targets, the month on one screen, and the most compact To do page (all four tasks and their Edit links in one screen) with legible porcelain type. It inherits the tiny frame-line tabs (ALL IDEAS | RESTAURANTS, LIST | MONTH), which hide the restaurants filter and the List view.

On Ideas the chosen 'All ideas' looks dark and off while 'Restaurants' looks raised and lit, and on Plans 'List' looks chosen when Month is. That breaks both 'where am I' and 'show only restaurants'. fixes.suggestion: Keep the one-line rows with leaders, the one-screen Home and month, Send on the From row, and the one-line Status and Settings lists. They are the best glance-reading in the round. Fix: (1) Below about 40rem, drop the head column above the rows with a 1.2rem head, so the phone Home is not three screens. (2) On the phone, let Vera's and the family's bubbles run from the gutter edge (no indent under the name), for 30+ characters a line. (3) Swap the VT323 field labels for Plex Mono caps at .75rem, 500 weight. (4) On To do, put Show before Search on one row, and hang 'was due 2 days ago' in amber as Home does, not '2026-09-27 19:56' (needs `late` in views.task_row). (5) Set All ideas / Restaurants as a horizontal tab pair directly over the rows (or give the head-column pair a 2px needle and 1rem type), so the filter sits beside what it filters. (6) Cap the facts column so 'in 2 days' is no more than about 12rem from the title at 1280, or pull the What it has cost band above Connected to on Status.

Keep the steel reverse block as the one 'here' mark everywhere, the square checkboxes with amber 'was due', the shaded weekends and the rail legends. Fix: (1) Make Earlier/Later bounded keys again: navigating the month is a primary action, not a rail link. (2) Fit the month on one screen as Programme Guide and Magic Eye do: shorter cells, events visible without scrolling. (3) In Chat, set each family message's time at its own bubble (right-aligned stop), not in a left gutter about 700px away. (4) On To do, hang relative 'was due 2 days ago' in amber in the margin, not ISO.

Keep the task-order Home (ask, then Coming up beside To do), Send on the From row and the brighter ink. Fix: cut the wide Next up scope to about 110px tall, or set it at the head of the Coming up column, so the lists rise back above the fold. Give the ways-to-start column the same height as the box, so it does not leave empty glass above the keys, and bring the last 3 small targets to 44px.

Keep the greige reverse block, the compact To do rows and the one-screen month. Legends stay for names; controls should look like controls.

Worth developing: tabs beside what they control (List/Month by the Plans title, the Ideas tabs in the list head) and Send on the From row are the right placements. Fix: (1) Make 'Add something to do' and 'Save a thought for later' bounded, filled disclosure buttons in sentence case again. A legend on a rule is a heading, so the page's main action disappears. (2) Keep amber for overdue only and show 'Open' neutral. (3) Draw the setup steps as rings or arrows, not empty squares that invite a tick. (4) Give the Search and Show labels one treatment.

Keep the compact heads (tabs, Save and Add in one Ideas head; Add and filter above the To do list). Make the to-do checkbox a square well with the ring beside it on the track as the stop, so a pressable thing never shares a shape with a decorative one. Add the `late` field so overdue shows amber on the To do page too.

Invert the latch: the chosen key should be the lit one (teal 2px cap, bright label, pressed 1px), and the unchosen keys the plain raised ones. Otherwise All ideas / Restaurants and List / Month read backwards. Also: bring targets to 2.75rem (41/56 small), lift ink to about 13:1, and set Coming up beside To do at 64rem or wider, so Home is not 2,300px with one row of ideas above the fold.

Keep the word labels for Memory, Family, Status and Settings in the desktop bar: they are the easiest to find in the round. Put the icons back beside the dots on the phone tab bar. Keep Newsreader for titles only and set body, chat and fields in a sans at 1rem. Use two columns at 64rem or wider, so Coming up and To do sit in the first screen and Status is not one long stack. Bring targets to 2.75rem and set SEND and FILTER in sentence case.
