judges.notes: Walked the family's tasks on each candidate. (1) Send a message: every box works. Send on the From row (Programme Guide, Flight Deck, Plotting Room Rehung, Magic Eye, Attract Mode, Porcelain Atlas) saves a line and keeps the eye on one row. (2) See what is on: Programme Guide and Magic Eye show Coming up, To do and Lately added within about a screen and a half. Porcelain Atlas and Attract Mode push Coming up to the bottom of or below the first screen. (3) Find an idea: Programme Guide shows 9 rows above the fold; Attract Mode and Porcelain Atlas lead with the radar and show one row or none. (4) Show only restaurants: the clearest tabs are Signal Legend's reverse block, Plotting Room's pills and Flight Deck's in-list pair. The frame-line tabs (Reverse Video, Bakelite Video) and the margin tabs (Magic Eye, Retitled) are small and far from the list. Attract Mode's latch is inverted and reads the wrong one as chosen. (5) Tick a to-do and see overdue: Home flags 'was due' in amber almost everywhere, but no candidate flags overdue on the To do page itself, which still prints ISO dates. This is a markup gap (views.task_row has no `late`) that every design should close at implementation. Ring checkboxes (Signal Galley, Signal Lines) are ambiguous next to decorative rings. (6) Find a date: the month fits on one screen in Magic Eye, Retitled, Programme Guide, Flight Deck, Reverse Video, Bakelite Video and Porcelain Atlas; the Signal family and Plotting Rooms still hide the current week below the fold. (7) Change a setting: Programme Guide's one-line list reads fastest, and Porcelain Atlas's single column is the longest. (8) Sign in is fine everywhere except Magic Eye's underline-only field. Targets: the Signal family, Reverse Video, Bakelite Video, Flight Deck and Programme Guide have 0 under 44px. Magic Eye, Retitled, Attract Mode and Porcelain Atlas are at today's 41-45/56. The first 18 Tab stops are identical everywhere, and moved controls beyond stop 18 are still unverified. The owner's test that the change reach the page content is met by all but the calmest refinements. Programme Guide changes Home below the fold, Ideas, Status, Settings and Plans most in ways a family member would feel as faster to read, not only different to look at. Suggested principle for the standard: a control never takes the shape of a label or a decoration (no action as a legend, no checkbox as a timeline ring, no tab set into a frame line), and the chosen state is always the lit one.

scores.why: Yardstick. Green on black with green in everything (83% share, the Matrix note), glare at 17:1, cards that all look alike, and 45 of 57 targets on Home under 44px. It is usable, but nothing in it helps you find things.

The biggest structural change that still reads as FamilyDB. One-line rows read across a leader to a facts column on Home, Status, Settings, Ideas and To do, so you take in each page at a glance (about 9 ideas above the fold, Settings as one clean list), with 0 small targets. Against it: the head links are spaced denim caps ('ALL PLANS', 'CHANGE A KEY') that read as labels, not links. Leaders run on to nothing on 'Renew library cards' and the wishes rows, VT323 field labels look pixelated at small size, heads wrap in the 10rem column, and To do's count is orphaned up in the head column.

The most legible Home of the round. Label-over-data rows, legends set in the demarcation lines, and each colour has one meaning: cyan links really look like links, and amber means caution. Skeptic's charges: the cyan is about 5 dE from Tokyo Night, so it risks reading as an editor theme. Mono caps legends are everywhere, and the disclosures ('SAVE A THOUGHT FOR LATER', 'ADD SOMETHING TO DO') became caps legends with no button affordance. On Status, 'on' is a loud green bar while 'off' is a tiny red notch. The setup links wear checkboxes.

The best-finished Signal Galley breed and the most usable at the controls. A steel reverse-video block makes 'you are here' unmistakable, ticks are square, rail links are underlined, and there are 0 small targets on every page. But above the fold it is a near-duplicate of Signal Galley. The steel is so low in chroma that Status and Chat slide back to 82-91% green share. The '=' end caps on the rails read as a perforated rule, and Chat's times sit about 800px from the family's bubbles.

Still sound: green-black slate, the fortnight line, the timetable margin, 0 small targets. It is now superseded by its own children. Status and Settings are Galley Rack copies, the round To do ticks read as radio buttons, today on the month is an amber disc (which breaks amber's one job), and Chat splits its times across two gutters.

Its windows and reverse video carry the period through grammar, and green share is 34%. But the mono-caps legends shout. Links set into the bottom frame ('All plans', 'Change a key', 'Add an idea · All 12') read as labels, a usability cost. The frames double up everywhere, and it is the least green entrant on Status.

Round 7 already found that lines on every page read as a git graph or subway map, and here they are on every page. Home above the fold is Signal Galley's. The To do ticks are rings on a track, so they look like timeline stops, not controls. 'You are here' in the bar is a 5px dot, which lessons.md calls too small, and the ring-and-buffer-stop heads on Status and Settings read as pins.

Safe and grounded, but the Status and To do strips are a grey admin-table mass, the board is invisible against black, and the periwinkle is the predictable identity. It is mostly Radar Room below the fold.

The rehang makes the pewter slab the owner criticised bigger: a full-width case with about 100px of empty glass. The ways to start become a sidebar-looking column that empties while you type. Home gets 170px longer, and every other page is the parent's with brighter text, against the calmer-ink brief.

The most beautifully typeset and most original page here: magnitude marks, star colours, one measured column. As a system to use it regresses. The lit glass greeting is gone. The nav swaps icons for 5px dots and tracked caps, which hurts recognition on the phone tab bar. 45 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, Home runs 2,942px, 60% of a desktop is empty, links are grey tracked caps, a serif body has faded in five rounds, and the starfield specks read as dust.

Keys that look pressable and wells that look typeable are good affordance. But the ground is lifted teal graphite (the highest mean luminance of the round, h169-194), the teal companion rounds 4-6 rejected. The full-width ruled bands read as a generic SaaS landing page. 41 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, and the focused select shows only a faint 1px sea-green edge, not the brand ring.

Reverse Video's grammar cut from oxblood leaves every window, dialog, bubble and the month grid maroon-brown. Squinted it is a red page with green lights: Christmas, with red off-rings on a red Status. The greige reverse block on the bar reads as a disabled grey pill, not 'you are here'.

Wine Bakelite and rose labels with the green read as Christmas or an alert. The bracket '[ Send ]' buttons are a gimmick, the hanging heads leave switched-off black, the Ideas tabs are stranded in the margin, and 43 of 56 targets are under 44px.

All of Magic Eye's faults remain. It adds the Fraunces serif (faded in rounds 5, 7 and 8) on the greeting and titles: heads now wrap ('What it / has cost') and the rose rules run out with no action at their end. Softening the text a step is invisible next to the costume.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the head column in the band, the one-line rows with a tabular facts column, the one-list Settings and the needle. Fix: make head links look like links (sentence case, underlined, denim #9db6d6, not .7rem spaced caps). Draw a leader only when a facts cell follows (`.row:not(:has(.facts:not(:empty))) .leader{display:none}`) and cap a row's measure (about 62rem, or the facts column right after a 3rem gap) so the eye does not cross 600px of dots. Replace the VT323 field labels with Plex Mono 500 .72rem .04em caps. Set heads at 1.3rem with `text-wrap:balance`, or widen the column to 11rem, so 'Finish setting up' stays on one line. Move 'N shown' into the band as the first row. Check why the third setup row is lit amber at rest (hover or focus only). Mark overdue To do rows amber on the To do page as on Home.

Keep the EFIS rule (each colour one meaning), the legends in the demarcation lines, the label-over-data rows and the cyan selection box in the bar. Fix: a disclosure must look pressable, so 'Save a thought for later' and 'Add something to do' go back to act plates with a sentence-case semibold label, chevron and plus, not caps legends. On Status, draw off the same way as on (a 2px dim-red or pewter bar), and keep the brand bar for live only. Take the cyan a step off the editor palettes (about #8fb3d6, C .06). Give setup items an arrow or ring instead of an empty checkbox. Cut legends to .72rem 500 at .04em.

Keep the steel reverse video for here, square family surfaces, legends and links set in the rails, and 0 small targets. Fix: give Home above the fold one visible change of its own (the thin squarer case is there; add the rail grammar to the greeting's ways to start, or steel the From row). Drop the '=' end caps on the rails. Hang the family's chat times in a right gutter beside their bubbles. Lift the steel to about C .055 so the companion registers on Status and Chat.

Keep the typographic scale, the magnitude marks (a disc for a part, a star for here), the star colours on rules and discs, and the porcelain-and-cobalt plates. Fix: restore the lit glass greeting pool. Keep the Lucide icons in the bar and tab bar, tinted with each part's star colour, with the disc as the 'here' mark. Use two columns at 72rem or more (Coming up beside To do, Lately beside Wishes) to halve the length. Make links underlined sentence case in the accent, not grey tracked caps. Bring targets to 44px. Keep Newsreader for h1 and h2 only, with Plex or DM Sans for body and rows. Drop or thin the starfield.

Keep one track where time runs (Home's fortnight, To do's due margin) and drop the rest. Put a square tick well beside each ring rather than making the ring the checkbox, and give the bar a latched cell for here instead of a 5px dot.

Keep the affordances: raised keys for actions and links like 'All plans', sunk wells for fields, one ruled band per section on Home. Put the ground back on green-black (#0d1210) with steel, not teal. Give the select `:focus-visible` the 2px brand ring, and bring targets to 44px.
Oxblood only where there is Bakelite (the monitor case, perhaps the foot). Put the windows on slate, and make the reverse block steel (#748a9b), not greige.

judges.notes:
The user's relayed word asks whether usability is being judged. Until now it has been, but only partly: the harness counts 44px targets and Tab order, and no lens has owned recognisability. I scored it inside the skeptic lens this round, and I recommend a dedicated usability judge. It would check whether a link looks like a link, a disclosure like a button, a tick like a tick, and 'you are here' like a latched cell; the focus rings on every control; scroll length; and how much of each page can be read at a glance.

Evidence from health.json: 0 of 56 Home targets under 44px in every informed entrant, Reverse Video and Bakelite Video. Signal Galley, Signal Lines and both Plotting Rooms have 1-9 on some pages. Magic Eye, Retitled, Attract Mode and Porcelain Atlas keep today's 41-45 of 56 (Porcelain Atlas has 52 of 97 on To do and 37 of 57 on the phone Home).

Recurring usability regressions this round: links and disclosures re-set as caps legends (Flight Deck, Programme Guide's head links, Reverse Video's frame links); controls redrawn as diagram marks (Signal Lines' rings as ticks, Flight Deck's setup checkboxes); icons removed from navigation (Porcelain Atlas); 'here' shown as a dot (Signal Lines). A principle worth adding to the standard: 'A control keeps the drawing people already know (box to tick, underline to follow, raised key to press); the period grammar dresses it and never replaces it.'

Colour: every red or wine companion (Magic Eye, Retitled, Bakelite Video) and the teal ground (Attract Mode) failed again, as rounds 4-8 predicted.

The breed worth trying next: Programme Guide's banded head column and one-line rows, with Flight Deck's colour-meaning code and label-over-data facts, and Signal Legend's steel reverse video for here.

designs.name: Attract Mode
designs.tagline: An arcade after hours: graphite cabinets stacked in ruled bands across the page, keys with a little travel, fields sunk as wells, a teal night light, and the green only where a screen is running.
designs.concept: The page is a dark arcade after closing. Graphite cabinets with a teal tint are stacked as full-width bands, each ruled from the next in its section's arcade-button colour. The only phosphor comes from the monitors, the mark, the Send key, the key word, focus and the live lights. It should feel quiet, solid and a little playful: raised things are keys you press, a key latched down means you are here, and sunk wells are where you type.
designs.companions: Teal at OKLCH hue 194 (#77cfce) is the main companion. It is the accent (links, the Home pill, the Status and Settings caps and rules, the Filter icon, the locate icon), the ambient, wash and top-glow, the label colour (#8db7b6: dates, eyebrows, times, relative days), the card edges (#27403f), the tint in surface and in Vera's bubble (#162222 / #142726), secondary text and the scroll bar. The ground is graphite at hue 169 (#101815), a step lighter than today. The section and kind colours are a lower-chroma set picked to stay apart for colour-blind sight: periwinkle plans #84b7f8, lilac ideas #a88fcf, pale brass to-do #e6dc98, amber people #e9ab66, rose shows #f2a4bf, brick seasons #d87e67 and sage outing #7ec08c. Each appears only in solid things with a job: the 2px band rule and page-head rule (70% of the section colour), an 8% spill under that rule (6% for the warm bands), a 7% tint in the page head, the flat heading caps, the month on the date chips, and the 3px kind edge on idea and task cards. The family's bubbles are slate (#252d31) against Vera's teal (#142726), with flat amber initials. `lit` is a calmer sea green (#76d8aa) for checkboxes, the box being typed in and done states.
decisions: Layout: stacked full-width bands. main is full width with padding that keeps a 70rem column and overflow-x: clip. Each band paints edge to edge from a ::before (inset 0 -100vmax), so there is no sideways scroll and no wrapper markup. The same rule holds on every page: the page head is a lit band, every top-level section.panel is a band (Home, Status, Chat, Settings), and the foot is the last band.

Home markup (variants/r9-rand-1/templates/home.html): the dashboard is split into bands for Coming up, To do and Lately added, each head's icon on a cap. The parent's card of the kids' wishes now comes after To do. The words are unchanged (3.7%, from the demo's missing chat line).

Section colour as structure, not glow: a 2px rule at 70% of the section colour, an 8% spill ending at 120px, and a 7% tint in each page head. Plans' head reads as periwinkle graphite, To do's as brass graphite and Ideas' as lilac graphite, where before all three were the same teal.

Controls follow one rule. Raised means press it: the green primary key has a 3px skirt and a real press, the graphite secondary keys and tabs have a 2px skirt. Latched down means you are here: the bar's current place, the current tab and the current settings item are dark and inset, moved down 2px. Sunk means type here: every field is a well with a darker top edge. Things you cannot press (heading caps, date chips, initials) are flat inlays with a 1px edge and an inner highlight, no skirt.

Type: Figtree for everything read, in steps: page titles clamp(2rem, 3.6vw, 2.6rem)/750/-0.03em, the question 30px/800, band heads 24px/750/-0.021em, card titles 17-18px/700, body 16/1.5, lede 17px at 58ch with text-wrap: pretty. Martian Mono at 80% width, uppercase at +0.1em, only for counted or labelled things: eyebrows, dates, times, relative days, ids, table heads, the brand and the foot. Names, counts and link legends are in Figtree. Times use tabular figures.

Status and every other page get the arcade caps without markup: `main h2 > svg.icon:first-child` gets content-box padding, a fill and an edge in the section colour, so Keys, Connected to, What it has cost, the Family and Memory headings and the kids' conversations all wear the same cap as Home's bands.
Icons are drawn at a 1.5 stroke. Motion is one faint scan line down each monitor's glass as it switches on (1.25s, from opacity 0 to a peak and back, removed under prefers-reduced-motion).
Pacing is on an 8px unit (8/12/16/24/32/40/48). Bands are 32 on top and 40 below; page heads are 32/24 with a 32px gap, or 24/16 on a phone.
Contrast: ink #c6d3d4 is 11.75:1 on bg, near the roll's 11 and softer than today's 17.1. Headings step up to #e3f0f0 (15.5:1), so hierarchy comes from lightness, not glow.
Sign-in exempts .narrow from the band rule and is drawn as a single cabinet: monitor above, controls below.
glow 0.49 and screenGlow 0.82 as rolled. The greeting has only a faint green bloom near the monitor and a teal corner wash, not the bottom-left glow.
designs.measures: Full render, 0 hard checks failed and 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 11.75, brand_on_bg 14.12, heading on bg 15.46, label on bg 8.23. Green share of colour: home 30.6%, ideas 82.0%, chat 52.2%, status 31.3%. Hue entropy: home 0.635, ideas 0.37, chat 0.345, status 0.207. Kinds dE typical/deutan/protan 18.1 / 7.4 / 7.5; sections 18.1 / 7.4 / 6.4 (tritan 5.2). The greeting corner (1150,120) samples (21,38,33): a teal, not bronze. Bottom-left (100,640) samples (16,24,21). Band tops under the new rules: setup (27,31,25), Coming up (28,41,43), To do (27,34,27), wishes (36,40,40), Lately added (26,32,34). Smallest text 11.52px, no sideways scroll, CSS 24,150 of 25,000 characters.
strengths: The change reaches all of Home's content, not a corner: a lit marquee greeting, then each section in its own full-width band, ruled in its section colour. The ground tones alternate and the foot is the last band.

The section colours now carry the structure. Plans, To do, Ideas, Status and Chat each open on a head tinted and ruled in their own colour, so the pages no longer share one teal header, and squinting separates Home's bands.

One coherent control grammar that holds on every page: raised keys to press, latched-down keys for where you are (bar, tabs, settings nav), sunk wells to type in, and flat inlays for caps, chips and initials that only label.
The first screen now shows content on every inner page. The month's five weeks and their events fit on Plans, Ideas shows its first row of kind-edged cards, and the chat starts higher.
The bright #6dff9c is kept to the mark, Send and Add, 'mind', focus, live lights and the monitors. Everything else is grounded teal-graphite with low-chroma section colours in solid things.
Typography with clear jobs: Figtree in real steps with tight large titles, Martian Mono narrowed only for dates, times, ids and eyebrows. Chat names now stand out from their timestamps.
weaknesses: The latched-down tab and settings item are dark, inset and 2px lower. At a glance that is close to the look of a field well, and a newcomer could read the current tab as disabled rather than chosen.
Ideas is still 82% green by share: even at 10rem the radar monitor is the largest coloured thing on the page, and only the first row of cards makes it above the fold.
The spill under each rule is still subtle. Squinted, the band colour comes mostly from the 2px rules and the caps, not the fields.
Next up is aligned to the ask deck by a fixed 50px top margin measured from the speaker line. If the speaker line wraps, or a kid's Home has no ask, they will drift apart.
On Status, the 'Who answers' heading carries Vera's presence glyph rather than a cap, so one of its headings breaks the cap rule.
The in-field mic is now a flat icon inside the well, which departs slightly from 'everything pressable is a key'. It was done to stop its skirt spilling over the Description well.
Settings cards and the filter panels stay boxed inside their bands rather than being banded themselves. That works, but the band idea is strongest on Home and Status.
The CSS is near its budget (24,150 of 25,000), which leaves little room to carry further refinements.
revisions: Page head: padding 32/24 with a 32px gap (24/16 on a phone). Titles are clamp(2rem, 3.6vw, 2.6rem) at 750 and -0.03em, the title cap is 40px, and month cells are 6rem. Plans now shows all five weeks with their events, and Ideas shows its first row of cards.
Bands are 32/40, down from 40/48; the monitors row on Status is 32/40, the greeting 40/48 (24/32 on a phone).

Section colours: the band and page-head rules are 2px at 70% of the section colour, the page head's first stop is tinted 7% with the page's accent, and the spill is 8% ending at 120px. I held setup and To do at 6%, not 8%, so the warm bands read olive-brass, not bronze (setup top samples 27,31,25).

Control grammar. Heading caps, date chips and chat initials are now flat inlays (a solid fill, 1px edge and inset highlight; no skirt or drop shadow). Tabs are no longer a sunk tray: each tab is a key. The current tab and the current settings-nav item are latched down (deck fill, --key-down, translateY 2px). The in-field mic has no shadow.

Mono only for counted things. Section link legends ('All plans', 'Add an idea', 'All 4'), '.count' ('12 ideas', '4 shown (up to 100).') and the chat speaker's name are in Figtree; the name is in ink at 700. These were taken out of the 80%-width list.

Every `main h2` whose first child is an icon gets the flat arcade cap in its section colour, with no markup. Status, Chat's kids' conversations, Family and Memory now match Home. Heads get min-height 34px so the Status columns line up.
Home markup: the parent's 'The kids' wishes' band moved after To do and is compacted to 24/32. The tones re-alternate: Coming up and the kids' wishes on the band tone, the rest on bg.
Declined in part: I did not move the kid's own 'My wishes'. docs/WISHES.md has it as the first thing on her Home, so only the parent's summary moved.

The radar bezel is now cabinet graphite #243130, not grey #2e3738. I also shrank the Ideas radar to 10rem, which cut the monitor by about 50px so the kind-edged cards come onto the first screen. That was my own change, following the same note.

Polish. The primary hover now changes only the face gradient, keeping the base shadows and saving characters. Setup links hover in ink rather than amber. Next up's bezel is top-aligned with the ask deck at desktop widths (both at y=151). In the Coming up tickets the relative day is pinned to the foot of each ticket, so the ragged heights read as intended.
crit: The page-head band pushes the content off the first screen on every inner page. `.page-head` padding is 48/40 plus a 40px margin, and the band runs y 60 to 235 (275 with a breadcrumb). At 1280x900, Plans shows no plan at all: the week of the 29th, with Pho Oregon and Silver Falls, starts below 900, where today's page shows it at 830. Ideas shows no idea card, only '12 IDEAS' at y 889. On the phone, Chat spends about 285 CSS px on the head before the first message. Fix: `.page-head { padding: 32px 0 24px; margin: 0 0 32px }`; `.page-head h1 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 3.6vw, 2.6rem); font-weight: 750 }` (800 at 50px is louder than the content under it); `@media (max-width: 40rem) { .page-head { padding: 24px 0 16px } }`; and `table.month td { height: 6rem }` so a five-week month and its events fit. On Home, move `.band` padding from 40/48 to 32/40 (still on the 8px unit) to shorten the long stack.

The section colours are too faint to tell one band from another. The band rules are 1px at 42% into --rule, and they sample as greys: Coming up (78,114,141), To do (119,130,100), the Ideas head (91,96,121). The 4-5% spill is invisible, and every `.page-head::before` is the same teal (22,36,34), with the 10% radial only reaching (25,38,37). Squinted, Home is one even teal-grey stack, and Plans, To do and Ideas have identical headers. Grounded fix, with no added glow: make the band `::before` border-top and the `.page-head::before` border-bottom `2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 70%, var(--rule))`. Tint the head's first gradient stop to `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 7%, #172624)` so Plans' header reads as periwinkle graphite and To do's as brass graphite. Set --spill to 8% but end it at 120px, not 180px. This costs almost no budget, since it only edits numbers.

Give the controls one rule: raised means press it, latched down means you are here, sunk means type here. The page breaks that rule now. The bar's current place is sunk (`.places a[aria-current]`), but `.tabs a[aria-current]` (All ideas, Month) and `.settings-nav a[aria-current]` (General) are raised keys, so the one item you need not press looks the most pressable. Things you cannot press also have key travel: the `.title-icon/.key-icon/.section-icon` caps (a `0 2px 0` skirt plus a drop shadow), the date `.chip` (--key-depth) and `.said-them .avatar` (an amber skirt). Fix: make the caps, chips and avatars flat inlays, keeping the fill, the 1px edge and `inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.08)` and dropping the skirts. Remove the sunk deck from `.tabs` and make each tab a key (`background: var(--key); border: 1px solid var(--key-edge); box-shadow: var(--key-depth)`). Latch the current tab, and the current settings-nav item, down with `background: var(--deck); box-shadow: var(--key-down); transform: translateY(2px)`. Also set `.field.can-dictate > button.mic { box-shadow: none }`: the in-field mic keeps --key-depth, and on the new-idea form its skirt spills across the bottom border of the Description well, next to the resize grip. Dropping the shadows frees about 250 characters of the 1,292 left.

Use mono only for counted things. Martian Mono, narrowed and in capitals, turns sentence text into code. The section key legends ('Add an idea', 'All plans', 'All 4') are 0.75rem mono. `.count` reads '4 SHOWN (UP TO 100).' and '12 IDEAS'. In chat, `.said-by` sets the name in the same mono capitals as the time ('27 SEP, 19:47 SAM', 'VERA 27 SEP, 19:48'), so the eye cannot find who spoke. Fix: `.section-head a, .section-links a, .brief-more a { font: 600 .875rem/1 var(--sans) }`; `.count { font: 600 .875rem/1.4 var(--sans); letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: none; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums }`; `.said-by strong { font: 700 .875rem/1 var(--sans); letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: none; color: var(--ink) }`, so the name is in Figtree ink and the time stays a mono label. Take those selectors out of the closing `:is(...) { font-stretch: 80% }` list, which also saves characters.

The heading caps only exist where the home.html variant wraps the icon in `.key-icon`. Status's section headings (Keys, Connected to, What it has cost, Models and prices, Waiting, Worth a look) show bare 18px teal line icons, so the 'every section has its arcade button' rule stops at Home. Fix it without markup, since an inline SVG takes padding and a background: `main h2 > svg.icon:first-child { box-sizing: content-box; padding: 7px; border-radius: 8px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, #172221); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 38%, #253534) }`. Every section heading on every page then gets the same flat cap in its section's colour.

Home: the kids' wishes band is 195px tall for two short rows ('Maya 0 open', 'Theo 0 open'), and it sits between Finish setting up and Coming up, pushing the plans down. In variants/r9-rand-1/templates/home.html, move the two `.home-wishes` sections after the To do band, so the order is plans, then tasks, then wishes. Compact it with `.home-wishes.band { padding: 24px 0 32px }` and `.home-wishes .section-head { margin-bottom: 12px }`. Re-alternate the tones by changing `.home-wishes, .home-todo { --tone: var(--band) }` to `.coming, .home-wishes`, so the stack still alternates bg and band after the move.

Ideas: the radar's `bezel` #2e3738 is the lightest large neutral on the page. It reads as a grey appliance frame around a full-width 1120x280 green glass, and with the idea cards pushed below the fold the page measures 87.7% green. Set the bezel token to the cabinet's own graphite, about #243130 (one step above surface-3), so the monitor sits in the cabinet. With fix 1, the first row of cards and their kind-coloured top edges comes onto the first screen, which is what balances the green on this page.

Smaller polish. The primary `button:hover` restates all four shadows (about 190 characters); change only the background on hover and let the base shadow stand. On the setup band, make `.setup a:hover` use `color: var(--ink)` rather than amber, so the amber stays in the cap, the rule and the rings. On Home, the Next up bezel's top (y≈142) floats 15px above the ask deck's top (≈157); align them with a margin-top on `.welcome .next-up`. In the Coming up tickets, pin `.rel` to the bottom of each ticket (`align-self: end` in the text column) so the ragged heights read as intended.

firstDraft.name: Attract Mode
firstDraft.concept: The page is a dark arcade after closing: graphite cabinets with a teal tint, each part of the page its own full-width band that is ruled from the next, and the only phosphor coming from the monitors, the mark, the Send key, the key word, focus and the live lights. It should feel quiet, solid and a little playful. Every control is something you could press (a key with travel) or type into (a sunk well). Each section has an arcade button's colour: its icon sits on a dark cap of that colour, its band is ruled in it, and the colour spills faintly down from the rule.

designs.name: Porcelain Atlas
designs.tagline: A star atlas set as a book: one centred column in Newsreader on a green-black dome, porcelain ink and cobalt hairlines, each part of the site a disc of its own star colour, the page you are on a star, and the phosphor kept for the console.
designs.concept: The page is a planetarium's star atlas, bound as a book. It is one centred 45rem reading column with the night round it for margins: a cobalt zenith at the top, a few fixed stars in the margins only, and a green airglow rising off the horizon rule under Home's greeting. Porcelain ink, cobalt plates and hairlines, and low-chroma star colours do the everyday work. Marks now follow an atlas's magnitude scale: a disc for each part, a smaller disc for each kind, and an eight-rayed star for the page you are on. The exact #6dff9c is the operator's console: the mark and cursor, 'mind', Send and the primary buttons, focus, the live lights and the monitors. It should feel quiet, typeset and calm, with the green switched on only where the machine is.
designs.companions: Cobalt porcelain (OKLCH hue 252) is the neutrals' breath and the page's structure. It shows in every plate's surface (#171e27), the bar (#121921), the hairlines and card edges (#2a3745), the labels (#9cb0cb, small tracked caps), the porcelain-white headings (#e2ecf7), and the accent (#accef4) for Home, Vera, Status and Settings (links, their discs and stars, the current-page ring). It is also Vera's chat glaze (#172230, with a cobalt left rule), the zenith glow on every page, the ambient light and the monitors' bezel (#3c4e66). Rules now take the tint of their own part: `--rule` is worked out on every element from that element's --accent, so a section's rule leans teal, straw, violet or rose. The section and kind colours are star colours by spectral class: violet Ideas (#b293e1), O-III teal Plans and trips (#6ac1cb), G-star straw To do (#ded88e, the second companion near hue 108), K-star orange for people, restaurants and today (#e9ad70), H-alpha rose for wishes and shows (#e397b8), M-star coral for the seasons (#df816d) and celadon for outings (#a4e0c8). They appear as the discs in the bar and on the phone's tab bar, the section and kind discs, the tab and current-page underlines, and the rules. A calm celadon-phosphor lit (#8edbaf) takes ticked boxes, the box being typed in, OK badges and 'changed'. The family's chat bubbles are dark teal slate (#131b1c) with a hairline, and their initials are now outlined in orange.
decisions: Kept the roll's structure whole: a single centred column, serif for titles and reading, sans for labels and controls, flat square controls, no icons beside words, still motion, airy pacing, DM Mono figures in lists. The colour half is kept too: cobalt 252, straw 108, a ground at hue 169 one step lighter (L 0.195), cool ink, ink at 13.95:1, glow 0.84, screenGlow 0.92.

The type system has three faces, each with one job. Newsreader is for everything read: h1 at 450 weight and clamp(2.3rem,5vw,3.05rem), Home's question up to 3.2rem, h2 at 1.45rem, list titles at 1.18-1.32rem, body at 17px/1.6, chat at 1.1rem/1.55, ledes at 1.22rem/380. Instrument Sans is for everything labelled or pressed, now set by ONE selector list: 600 0.72rem/1.3, 0.13em, uppercase for the bar, tabs, the settings index, labels, eyebrows, kinds, said-by, counts, section links, and the owner names in both to-do lists. DM Mono (tabular) is for dates, times, ids, due dates and table figures, with slashed zeros only on times and ids, not on day numerals.

Marks are an atlas's magnitude scale, which replaces the four-point stars that read as '+'. Magnitude 2 is a 0.5rem filled disc at full colour before each place in the bar and tab bar, each section and panel head, each settings row and the restaurants link. Magnitude 3 is a 0.42rem disc before each kind. Magnitude 1 is an eight-rayed star (a 16-point polygon, long cardinal rays and short diagonals) beside the page title and on the phone's current tab. On the desktop bar the current page is a ringed disc (2px of bar, then a 1px accent ring). Vera's link and Home have their own cobalt accent in the bar, so the colour key reads the same on every page.

One rule for every page: lists are ruled, groups sit on plates. Home's agenda, checklist, ideas and wishes were already ruled. The Ideas and Restaurants lists, the To do page and the Plans list are now ruled catalogues too: hairline rows, the idea number set at the right like a catalogue number, and a 2.8rem hanging indent on tasks so each body lines up with its title. Forms, filters, Status readouts and Finish setting up stay on cobalt plates with one hairline and a faint glaze at the top edge. Plates that are stripped also drop their glaze, so no ghost rules are left.

Home is a title page: Vera's small screen, VERA and the date in tracked caps, the question set large with only 'mind' glowing, a bare square field, and Send as the only filled green control. Serif ways to start sit in hairline boxes. Next up is a plate wider than the column, and a horizon rule with a green airglow closes the greeting.

The monitors are the phosphor's home and the only things allowed to break the measure. From 64rem wide, Next up and On the radar take -3.5rem of margin each side (about 52rem), so the radar's lines no longer wrap. The Status readout stays inside its plate.

Dates are set as a star catalogue. The day is large DM Mono, 2ch wide and right-aligned so OCT/THU stack in one column. The month is in Plans teal, the title is serif, the time is mono in ink-2 and 'in 2 days' is in the label colour.

Controls are flat and technical: square, one hairline, and a fill only on press, except the single filled green primary. Checkboxes and radios are drawn by hand and fill with lit. Keyboard focus is a 1px #6dff9c outline offset 3px with a faint halo, and the checkbox now gets it too through its own :focus-visible rule. The Ideas filter is quiet (quietFilter). Tabs and the settings index are running heads with an accent underline.

The Plans month is a full-width plate (62rem) and the one planned exception to the measure. The star mask widens with it, the plate's padding is gone, cells are 5.5rem, and the head is tightened, so the whole month and its plans fit on a 900px screen. Events are set in serif with a teal left rule.

Measure: running text in plates, source notes, hints and descriptions are capped at 32em (about 75 characters), and chat lines at 36em. The time-zone note under a page head is pulled up to the lede (1.1rem) and given 2rem before the first plate.

The planetarium ground is a cobalt zenith and a sparse field of 1px stars fixed behind the page and masked out of the column, now written in 8-digit hex to save budget. There are none on a phone. The ground stays green-black (#0f1714).

Broken guidelines, with reasons: the month plate and the two monitors break the measure because seven days and a radar need the width. The settings side nav is an inline table of contents. Home's welcome is not a lit card, so the corner 'wash' role barely shows and the zenith and airglow do its work. Everything is CSS (24,875 of 25,000 characters); no template variant was needed.
designs.measures: Final full render (./check.sh palettes/r9-rand-2.json): 0 hard checks failed, 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 13.95:1; brand_on_bg 14.25:1 (brand exactly #6dff9c, neon 1.0x today). Green share of colour: home 23.9%, ideas 46.2%, chat 28.7%, status 12.1% (today 66-96%). Hue entropy: home 0.385, ideas 0.322, chat 0.324, status 0.222. Bright-green permille: home 1.75, ideas 7.67, chat 2.6, status 0.07. CIEDE2000 kinds: typical 15.6 (outing~trip), deuteranopia 6.3, protanopia 6.0. Sections: typical 16.8 (home~plans), deuteranopia 6.3, protanopia 6.0. Smallest text 11.52px; no sideways scroll on any page; words unchanged. Greeting corner pixels on home.png: (1150,120) = (15,23,20) and (100,640) = (15,23,20). Both are the plain green-black ground, because the greeting is no longer a card with a wash. The zenith at top centre (640,60) samples (20,31,36), a cool blue, and the airglow above the horizon rule (640,760) samples (19,39,29), a green. CSS is 24,875 of the 25,000 characters.
strengths: It is the most distinct entrant: a typeset book page with a night sky round it, unlike the panel-and-grid apps. The difference from today shows on every page, not in one corner.

A coherent system with rules that hold everywhere. There are three faces with three jobs, one small-caps voice from a single selector list, lists ruled and groups on plates (Home, Ideas, Restaurants, To do, Plans list and Settings all follow it), and one magnitude scale for every mark.

Green is held to the console: the mark, 'mind', Send and the primary buttons, focus, the live lights and the monitors. Everything else is grounded cobalt porcelain and low-chroma star colours with jobs.

Typographic care: balanced serif headings, a 75-character measure in plates, tabular mono figures in a right-aligned day column, hanging indents on tasks, and the time-zone note set as part of the head.
The colour key is back in the bar and on the phone's tab bar as full-colour discs, with a ringed disc or an eight-rayed star for where you are. Nothing reads as '+'.
The whole Plans month, with its plans, fits on one 900px screen, and the radar's lines no longer wrap.
weaknesses: The airy pacing makes Home long (2,942px at 1280), and a To do row is still about 160px because 'No active reminder.' and 'Edit, complete, or snooze' each take a line.
The CSS budget is almost spent (24,875 of 25,000), so there is no headroom for further fixes without cutting something.
The magnitude-1 star (1.3rem) is small and thin beside a 3rem title. It reads as a sparkle rather than a strong mark, and it cannot glow because clip-path clips any shadow.

The wishes page (.cards.wishes) was deliberately left on plates because of its dragging, and the Family, Memory and single-idea pages were not rendered or checked. The 'ruled lists' rule may not hold there yet.
The month grid is still a field of uniform cobalt cells. Weekends and days outside the month are only faintly told apart, and long event titles wrap in the narrow cells.
Status is still a stack of plates. Its 'Worth a look' dates are in serif, not mono, which breaks the figures rule in one place.
The wash and ambient tokens barely show, because the greeting is not a card. The page's second light is the zenith, which is subtle at the sampled pixels.
On a phone, Vera's reply still sets about 33 characters a line, even with the smaller outlined initials and tighter bubble padding.
`--rule` is worked out on every element (`* { --rule: ... }`) so each rule can take its own part's tint. That is a small styling cost on every element.
revisions: Marks (fix 1): the four-point '+'-like stars are replaced by an atlas magnitude scale. Parts and panel heads get 0.5rem full-colour discs, kinds get 0.42rem discs, and settings rows and the restaurants link get discs. The desktop bar's current page is ringed (0 0 0 2px bar, 0 0 0 3px accent) instead of scale(1.3). The page title and the phone's current tab get an eight-rayed 16-point star. The 0.5 opacity on nav marks is deleted, and Vera and Home get their own cobalt accent in the bar so the key does not change colour from page to page. The settings nav's presence glyph is shrunk to 0.7rem with no glow.

Ghost rules (fix 2): `.panel.plain, .home-wishes, .idea-card, .cards > .card, .panel:has(> .agenda)` now drop the plate's inset top highlight and glaze gradient, and the idea-card hover rule comes after them. Home no longer has a doubled rule under Coming up, To do or Lately added, or above The kids' wishes.

To do (fix 3): tasks are a ruled list (gap 0, a rule in the part's tint above the list, hairline under each row, no plate). The owner is in tracked caps as on Home, the due date is in DM Mono, and '4 shown' is set like an eyebrow instead of mono. The time-zone note is pulled up under the lede with 2rem before 'Add something to do'. I also added a 2.8rem hanging indent so each task's body lines up with its title. I used `span:nth-child(3)` for the due date rather than the suggested `:last-child`, because the status tag is the last child when a task has no due date.

Plans month (fix 4): the star mask widens for the 62rem month so no star falls inside it. `table.month.panel` has no padding. Day numerals and chip days are tabular without slashed zeros. The head is tightened (1.5rem under the page head), cells are 5.5rem, and events are in serif with the teal left rule. The whole month, with its plans, fits on the 900px screen.

Measure (fix 5): `.panel p, .source, .hint, .description` are capped at 32em and `.said-text` at 36em. `.chip-day` is 2ch wide and right-aligned, so the month and weekday stack in one column (the day numeral is also back to 400, since DM Mono ships no 300).
Checkbox focus (fix 6): `input:is([type=checkbox],[type=radio]):focus-visible` now gives a 1px #6dff9c outline, offset 3px, with a green border. The focus-14 shot shows it clearly.

Monitors (fix 7): from 64rem wide, `main .next-up, main .on-radar` take -3.5rem of inline margin. I scoped it to those two rather than every `main .crt`, so the Status spend readout stays inside its plate. On the radar's lines now sit on one line each, and nothing scrolls sideways.

Avatars and setup (fix 8): the family's initials are outlined in orange rather than filled. On a phone they are 1.4rem with a 0.45rem gutter, and bubbles have tighter padding. 'Finish setting up' sits on the cobalt surface with a 2px orange left rule instead of the grey mix.

Budget (fix 8, continued): the ten repeats of the small-caps declaration are folded into one selector list, the star field is rewritten in 8-digit hex, the text-field selector is shortened to `input:not([type=checkbox],[type=radio],[type=hidden])`, and the comments are cut down. That made room for the new rules.

Beyond the notes: the Ideas and Restaurants lists and the Plans list page were still one heavy plate per entry, and the Ideas list drew two marks on each entry. They are now ruled catalogues matching Home, with the idea number at the right like a catalogue number. Each section's rule now takes that section's own tint. I also fixed the From label, which a base rule had been enlarging so that Send wrapped onto its own line on a phone.

Declined in part: 'drop the first `:root { --label; --heading }` line' as written. The theme does not define those variables, and my css reads var(--label) and var(--heading), so dropping them would fall back to dim and ink. I folded them, with a new --bar, into the main :root block instead, which saves the same characters. No other notes were declined.
crit: The marks read as '+', an add sign, and the bar loses its colour key. At 8-10px the --star polygon (waist 39%/61%) renders as a plus. It sits right beside 'ADD AN IDEA' on Home's Lately added, before every .section-head h2 and .panel > h2, and before each kind. In the bar, `nav a::before { opacity: 0.5 }` greys the section colours out as well, so once the icons are clipped the page has no colour key left (bar zoom: '+ VERA + IDEAS'). Fix: make the marks an atlas magnitude scale. For .places a::before, .section-head h2::before, .panel > h2::before and .kind::before use filled discs (clip-path: none; border-radius: 50%; 0.5rem, 0.42rem for .kind) at full colour, and delete the 0.5 opacity. Mark the current page with a ring (box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--bar), 0 0 0 3px var(--accent)) instead of scale(1.3). Keep a real star only at magnitude 1 (.title-icon and the current phone tab), drawn as an 8-point star with long cardinal rays and short diagonals (a 16-point polygon) so it cannot pass for a plus. Also shrink the lit presence glyph in .settings-nav, which sits mid-row between LOOKUPS and PERSONALITY on General as the heaviest thing in the nav.

Ghost double rules. `.panel { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(226 236 247/.05); background-image: linear-gradient(...) }` survives on every plate the page strips: .panel.plain (Home's .agenda and .checklist), .home-wishes and .idea-card (all are class panel in home.html). The result is a second faint rule about 19px under each Home section-head rule: Coming up at y≈1443, To do at y≈1898, and Lately added broken into two column stubs. Another faint rule crosses just above 'The kids' wishes' (y≈1141). Fix: add `.panel.plain, .home-wishes, .idea-card { box-shadow: none; background-image: none }` and put .idea-card:hover's inset rule after it.

The To do page is not carried. Each task is a full plate (li.panel.card.task), 184px tall, so a screen shows one and a half tasks, while Home's To do is a ruled list. The figures rule is also inverted there: 'Due 2026-09-27 19:56' is in serif, but the sentence p.count '4 shown (up to 100).' is in DM Mono. Fix: `.tasks { gap: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule) } .tasks > .task { padding: 1.1rem 0; background: none; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); box-shadow: none }` and `.task .meta > span:last-child { font: 400 .85rem var(--mono) }` (the due date). Take .count out of the mono selector list and set p.count like .eyebrow. Give the time-zone note ('Times use America/Vancouver…') 1.4rem of air above 'Add something to do': today it sits 8px from that plate and 60px from the lede.

Plans month. First, the star mask (`--m` on body::before) is cut for 45rem, but the month is 62rem wide, so a star shows inside the content: a speck under LIST at (172,262). Second, table.panel.month keeps the plate's padding and spacing, so the grid floats about 6px inside its own frame. Third, slashed zeros turn '10 / 20 / 30' into Ø. Fourth, the title, tabs, source note and 'September 2026' take 370px before the grid, so the first screen shows no plan at all. Fix: `body:has(table.month)::before { --m: linear-gradient(90deg,#000 calc(50% - 36rem),transparent calc(50% - 32rem),transparent calc(50% + 32rem),#000 calc(50% + 36rem)) }`, `table.month.panel { padding: 0; border-spacing: 0 }`, and `table.month time, .chip-day { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums }` (keep slashed-zero for times only). Tighten `.in-plans .page-head` to a 1.5rem bottom margin and the cells to about 5.5rem, so six weeks and their events fit on a 900px screen.

Measure and figures. At 17px Newsreader in a 45rem column, running text inside plates sets about 95 characters a line (General's 'It decides the forecast…' help, the Status notes, task notes), well past a book page's 60-75. On Home's Coming up, .chip-day's width moves the month column: 'OCT' starts about 17px further right after 17 than after 1. Fix: `.panel p, .source, .hint, .description { max-width: 32em }` (about 75 characters; .lede already has 34em) and `.said-text { max-width: 36em }`. Add `.chip-day { min-width: 2ch; text-align: right }` so OCT and THU stack in one column under every date.

Checkbox focus is invisible. The base `input:focus { outline: none }` (specificity 0,1,1) beats your `:focus-visible` rule (0,1,0), and your later `input[type="checkbox"]` rule (also 0,1,1) resets the border to --edge. Tabbing onto 'Send where I am' therefore shows only a 14% green haze (the focus-14 shot), which fails the focus floor. Fix: `input:is([type=checkbox],[type=radio]):focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--green); outline-offset: 3px; border-color: var(--green) }`.

The monitors are cramped by the measure. Ideas' On the radar wraps 'Nearest #7 Pumpkin patch at Bi-Mart / farm [18 MIN NW]' and its note over two lines each. The monitors are the phosphor's home, and in an atlas a plate may break the measure. Fix: `@media (min-width: 64rem) { main .crt { margin-inline: -3.5rem } }`. That makes Next up and On the radar about 52rem wide, centred on the column, as the only things that break it. Nothing scrolls sideways, because main has at least 7rem of margin at that width.

Loud avatars and a grey setup plate. `.said-them .avatar { background: var(--people) }` makes solid orange 36px squares, the loudest objects in the thread and louder than Send. On the phone the avatar gutter leaves Vera's reply about 30 characters a line. Home's .setup mixes 5% people into the cobalt surface, which cancels to a flat grey (34,37,43), so it is the dullest object on Home and reads as disabled. Fix: outline the avatars in their colour (background: none; border: 1px solid var(--people); color: var(--people)), and under max-width 30rem make them 1.4rem with a narrower gutter. Put .setup on var(--surface) with a 2px border-left in --people, or 9% people on --surface-2. To make room at 23.7k of 25k: fold the roughly ten repeats of `font: 600 0.72rem/1.3 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .13em; text-transform: uppercase` into one selector list, and drop the first line `:root { --label; --heading }`, which duplicates the tokens.

firstDraft.name: Porcelain Atlas
firstDraft.concept: The page as a planetarium's star atlas, bound as a book. It is one centred reading column (45rem) with the night all round it for margins: a cobalt zenith at the top, a few faint fixed stars in the margins, and a green airglow rising off the horizon rule under Home's greeting. The four carried entrants are panel-and-grid apps; this one reads like a quiet, typeset page. Porcelain ink, cobalt glaze and star-coloured marks do the everyday work, and the exact #6dff9c is the operator's console: the mark and cursor, "mind", Send and the primary buttons, focus, live lights and the monitors.

designs.name: Magic Eye, Retitled
designs.tagline: The same thirties wireless set, its page titles now set in a soft Fraunces on one ruled line of sight with their one action, and every word a step easier on the eye.
designs.concept: This is Magic Eye with three rolled changes. Its titles are now printed like the cover lines of a 1930s radio programme magazine. Every page head is one line you read from left to right: the page's tile, a soft Fraunces title, a dusty-rose rule and the page's one action. All text is one step calmer, so the wine Bakelite, the porcelain type and the single green magic-eye tube feel warmer and quieter than the parent, not brighter.
designs.companions: No colour moved except the text. The companions are still the parent's: wine Bakelite in the cards, the chat bubbles and the monitor cases; porcelain in the titles; old rose in the labels; a sage accent; and the rose needle on the tuning scale. The only new colour is the head rule, a dusty rose made from the rose label mixed 34% into the wine line colour. It samples (107,74,89) and runs through every page head and the Plans month head. #6dff9c stays on the mark, Send and the primary buttons, the key word "mind", focus, the live lamps and the monitors.
decisions: Softer text (colour roll): I lowered OKLCH lightness and kept each hue. Ink goes from #ede3e6 to #dfd6d8 (15.07 to 13.28:1). Heading and --porc go from #f4ebe7 to #e5ddd9 (16.1 to 14.1). ink-2 goes to #c4b7bb (10.8 to 9.8), the rose label and --rose to #c793a8 (7.9 to 7.35), and dim to #a7949a (6.98 to 6.61). Faint stays at #99868d so the smallest text keeps 5.08:1 or more (lessons: keep the smallest text at 5:1 or above). The card titles and the bar's current place follow --porc, so the whole page is calmer, not only the body text.

Page heads (structure roll): each page head is now one wrapping flex line. The tile comes first, then the title, then a rule that grows to fill the space (a ::after with flex 1 1 1.25rem and a 1px border so it stays crisp), then the page's actions. A full-width ::before forces the lede onto its own line. I put `display:contents` on .page-title, so no markup had to change and the variant's words, forms and Tab order are exactly the parent's. The rule and the action's centre sit on the title's x-height centre, with a margin of clamp(.55rem,1.1vw,.8rem). Crumbs become a rose kicker above the title. Where a page has no action (Status, Chat, Plans, Settings, To do), the rule runs to the right edge. On a phone, an action too wide for the line wraps below the title rather than breaking a word.

On desktop the title hangs from the page edge at x=32, like the parent's band heads, while the lede stays on the column at x=260 with the content below it. This keeps Magic Eye's programme-guide grid: heads hang left and everything you read sits in the column. The parent's bottom rule under the whole head, and the tile hung in the margin, are gone because the one rule now lives on the title's line.

I carried the same head drawing to the Plans month head. September 2026 is followed by a rule and then Earlier and Later, using flex order on a ::after. That makes 'title, rule, actions' the one rule for every head that has actions.

Serif (typography roll): Fraunces at weight 400 with SOFT 50 and WONK 0, optical size automatic, 2.4-3.45rem, letter-spacing -.02em, line-height 1. I chose Fraunces over Newsreader after rendering both. The soft old-style shapes belong to the set's era (Windsor and Souvenir are Fraunces's models), while Newsreader at 500 read as a modern newspaper. I kept the weight light and the softness at half because lessons.md says heavy Fraunces reads chunky or toy-like.

Where I broke a lesson on purpose: the serif also sets Home's greeting (it is Home's h1, so it is Home's page title) at weight 420, and Magic Eye's hanging heads at 1.6rem (Coming up, To do, Lately added, the kids' wishes, Finish setting up, What it has cost), plus the month head. In the parent, the page titles and hanging heads were one voice, and Home has no other title. Setting only the h1s would have left Home looking exactly like the parent. Panel heads, card titles, labels, the brand name, Vera's name, the date numerals and everything the machine says stay in the parent's sans and mono. The result is four steps: serif display 3.45, serif head 1.6, sans panel head 1.15, sans caps label .74.

Everything else is the parent's, unchanged: tokens, glow numbers, the tuning-scale bar, zebra timetable rows, bracket buttons, fields and bezels. I only removed parent rules the new head made redundant (the absolute margin tile and crumb offsets), which keeps the css at 24,045 of 25,000 characters.
designs.measures: Full render, 0 hard checks failed and 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 13.28 (parent 15.07); heading on bg 14.12; ink-2 on bg 9.76; label on bg 7.35; dim on bg 6.61; faint on surface 5.08; ink on bubble and bubble-them 12.15 and 9.43; ink on the bar 13.17; brand_on_bg 14.8. Brand is exactly #6dff9c. Green share of colour: Home 25.3%, Ideas 31.6%, Chat 12.1%, Status 21.5%. Hue entropy: .579, .423, .28, .42. Kinds dE, typical / deuteranopia / protanopia: 13.5 / 5.3 / 6.4. Sections: 15.6 / 5.3 / 6.5 (all unchanged from the parent). Greeting pixels: (1150,120) samples (8,16,12), which is on the Next up monitor's glass (the parent's layout puts the tube there), and (100,640) samples (14,18,12), the black ground. As in the parent there is no wash or glass pool. No sideways scroll on any page. Smallest text 11.52px. The head rule samples (107,74,89).
strengths: The roll is visible on every page at a glance. Ideas, Chat, Status, To do, Plans, Settings, General, the new-idea form, Sign in and the 404 all get a serif title on one ruled line. Home gets a serif greeting and serif hanging heads, so it looks different below the fold as well.

One head rule holds on every page: tile, title, rule, action. It covers pages with an action (Ideas, Family), pages without one (the rule runs to the edge), sub-pages (crumbs as a kicker) and the Plans month head (title, rule, Earlier and Later). Long titles wrap and the rule drops beneath them.

The type now has clear steps. Warm serif is for titles and heads, the parent's sans for panels, cards and body, rose caps for labels, and VT323 or mono only on the machine. The serif fits the set's 1930s programme-magazine idea better than it would fit any other family in the field.
The text is a step calmer (13.3:1 ink, 14.1:1 titles) and the smallest text stays at 5:1 or more, which answers 'too contrasty' without greying the black or touching the signature.
The markup is exactly the parent's (only css moved), so words, forms, Tab order and the details strip carry over unchanged.
weaknesses: Serif titles have faded in rounds 5, 7 and 8, and Fraunces was called toy-like. Even at weight 400 with SOFT 50, some judges will say it pulls the page off the CRT. Setting the greeting in the serif breaks the lesson 'never the greeting' on purpose.

The serif is wider than the parent's condensed sans, so several hanging heads now wrap to two lines in the 12rem margin: Finish setting up, The kids' wishes, What it has cost, The kids' conversations.
On desktop the title hangs from x=32 while the lede starts at x=260. Without the margin's context below, that step can look arbitrary on pages with little in the margin, such as Status and Settings.
To do's real action (Add something to do) is a details panel further down, so its head has no action and the rule simply runs out. I could not move it without changing the markup and the form.

The parent's faults are all still here, because the roll did not touch them: wine Bakelite and old rose beside the red off lamps (a Christmas or alert risk), no lit glass greeting pool, the pewter-free oxblood cases, many targets under 44px (Home 43 of 56, To do 46 of 97), and the parent's empty slack under the kids' wishes band.
Softening the text by one step is subtle. The family may feel it rather than see it next to the much larger change in the titles.

designs.name: Plotting Room, Rehung
designs.tagline: Plotting Room with Home rehung: Next up leaves the greeting for a wide scope hung across the room above the strip racks, the bays pair up in rows with their heads on one line, the ways to start stand as keys beside the box, and the type reads a step clearer.
designs.concept: This is a mutant of Plotting Room. In a plotting room the plot hangs on the wall and the strip racks sit below it, and Home is now laid out the same way. The greeting keeps only the machine's words: her question, the box, and the ways to start as a column of keys beside it. Next up becomes a wide chinned scope across the whole page that reads like a departures record. Below it the bays are paired in rows, the family's time (Coming up beside To do) above its things (Lately added beside the kids' wishes and somewhere to eat). The idea is to read the plot first and the racks second, calm and in order. All text is also set one contrast step clearer.
designs.companions: These are the parent's colours, unchanged. Periwinkle #a3aef5 marks where you are and what you can press (links, the current place, the family's bubble edge and the phone pill). Cobalt #4f60e6 is the greeting's second light at the top right, sampled at (26,34,49). Slate (#1a2025 strips, #11171c trays, #222a35 designators, #10151a bar) sits under every list, and the Plotting Room CSS gives each designator a small tint of its kind's colour. Pewter #44494f is the scope cases. Sage #86d9a6 is lit, done and today. The exact #6dff9c appears only on the mark, Send, "mind", focus, the live lamps and the monitors. The text roles (label #a9b6d2, heading #f1ece0, secondary #bec4db) are one step brighter but keep the parent's hues.
decisions: Roll 1 (colour), sharpen the text contrast by one step: every text role was lifted in OKLCH lightness with its hue and chroma kept. ink #d4cfc4 to #dcd7cc (12.49 to 13.52:1 on bg), ink-2 #b6b1a7 to #bdb8ae (9.09 to 9.87), dim #9f9b92 to #a6a299 (7.0 to 7.6), faint #928e85 to #99958b (5.8 to 6.31 on field), heading #ebe6da to #f1ece0 (15.58 to 16.4), label #a2afcb to #a9b6d2 (8.81 to 9.55), secondary #b7bdd3 to #bec4db (8.79 to 9.51 on surface). The parent's :root copies of --label, --heading and --secondary in its css were changed to match. This goes against lessons.md's 'ink near 12:1 reads calmer', and it is done only because the dice rolled it. At 13.5 the ink still sits well under today's 17.1.

Roll 2 (structure), rearrange Home, part 1, the monitor full width above the lists: in the variant's home.html, Next up's crt moves out of the greeting and becomes its own full-width band between the greeting and the setup panel. It stays at y 462-682 on desktop, so Next up is still above the fold. At 64rem and up the tube is set as a record: the NEXT UP tab, then the title at 2.6rem with a dotted phosphor leader running to a tab stop, then the when and '> 4 more on the radar' in a second column, with the 9rem radar at the end. The leader is switched off when there is no when line. The title may wrap in the wide tube (it no longer inherits the parent's nowrap), and the chin's vents were lengthened to 5.5rem to suit the wider case.

Roll 2, part 2, a different column structure for the greeting: without the scope beside it, the box would have run 1030px wide with nothing next to it. So at 64rem and up the greeting is a two-column grid: the box in a 1fr column, and the three ways to start stacked beside it in a 16.5rem column as full-width slate keys, bottom-aligned with the box's Send row. Below 64rem the greeting stacks as the parent's did. The green glass pool still rises behind the box, sampled at (100,400) = (32,51,38).

Roll 2, part 3, a different order for the lists: the parent racked everything in two columns read top to bottom. The board is now a grid of two rows of two bays, read row by row, and the DOM order was rewritten so Tab order matches that reading order (no dense packing, no CSS order). Row 1 is the family's time: Coming up beside To do, directly under the plot that its '4 more on the radar' link points to. Row 2 is its things: Lately added beside a column holding the kids' wishes and, under them, the 'Something to eat' plate, which moved out of Lately added to balance the row. Row 2's two columns end about 40px apart.

Heads on one baseline: the 'Google Calendar is not connected' source note moved below the Coming up rack as a footnote, set .84rem on the strips' left edge, so the Coming up and To do racks start on the same line.

Everything else is the parent's and was not changed: the strips, trays, rails, kind-tinted designators, Plex Sans with Plex Mono, keys, focus rings, the scope cases and all other pages. No words were added, dropped or rewritten, and lint_variant passes.
designs.measures: Final full render (./check.sh palettes/r9-mut-2.json): 0 hard checks failed, 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 13.52 (parent 12.49), brand_on_bg 15.18, smallest text dim on surface-3 about 5.6 and faint on surface about 5.4 (parent 5.22 and 5.03). Green share / hue entropy: home 35.0% / 0.58, ideas 58.7% / 0.547, chat 71.8% / 0.478, status 60.4% / 0.556 (parent 34.4 / 59.0 / 71.7 / 60.2). Kinds dE typical/deutan/protan 13.6 / 5.5 / 7.4; sections 12.6 / 5.0 / 7.4. Greeting corner pixel (1150,120) = (26,34,49), the cobalt wash (parent (26,34,50)). The green pool is sampled at (100,400) = (32,51,38); (100,640) now lands on the plot's glass, (3,7,6). Home desktop is 1914px tall (parent 1742). 3 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, the same as the parent. No overflow anywhere; smallest words 11.52px. CSS is 21,411 of 25,000.
strengths: The change shows on Home at a glance, from the greeting down to the last rack. None of the carried four hangs Next up as a full-width plot: Signal Galley spreads Coming up full width, Reverse Video and the parent use two columns, and Magic Eye uses stacked bands.

The sight line is clearer: ask, then the plot (what is next), then its '4 more on the radar' racked directly below, with To do beside it, so the two most useful lists sit together right under the scope.

Heads share one baseline in each row and both racks in a row start on one line, because the source note became a footnote. Tab order matches the row-by-row reading because the DOM was reordered rather than rearranged with CSS order.

The wide tube reads as a real plotting display: a departures-board record with a dotted phosphor leader to a tab stop, and a big VT323 title. The scope glass got larger while the bright-green pixel count on Home fell slightly (2.88 per mille against the parent's 3.13).
The ways to start as a column of keys beside the box use the width the scope left, and put the box's own bar (From, Send where I am, mic, Send) on one row.
weaknesses: Home is about 170px longer on desktop (1914 against 1742), because the scope now takes its own band instead of sharing a row with the box.

The full-width pewter case makes the grey slab more prominent. That is the case the owner already criticised in round 8, and it is still the parent's 10px-rim, 16px-radius case: only the vents were lengthened, and the thinner, squarer case lessons.md asks for is not attempted.
The wide tube has spare glass between the when column and the radar (about 100px) and between a short title and its tab stop, which the dotted leader only partly fills.
On the phone the change is small: the scope now sits on black outside the greeting glass, and the kids' wishes come before the restaurant plate. Above the fold the phone looks much like the parent.
The contrast roll works against lessons.md's calmer 12:1 ink. At 13.5 the page reads a touch closer to 'today with a tint', and the step is subtle enough that some judges may not notice it.
Chat, Ideas, Status, Plans, To do and Settings differ from the parent only by the brighter text. Their structure is exactly the parent's, which is what the roll allows.
With the ways to start in a side column, the greeting's upper right is empty dark glass above the keys. The keys also step aside while someone is typing (ask.js), which empties that column.

designs.name: Bakelite Video
designs.tagline: Reverse Video's windows, dialogs and reverse-video selection cut from Magic Eye's oxblood Bakelite and set in porcelain type, with the green of the magic-eye tube the one light that glows.
designs.concept: A text-mode program running inside a 1930s wireless set. It uses Reverse Video's grammar: square windows with their names knocked into the frame line, double-framed dialogs for what you act in, unboxed rows walked by a highlight bar, a reverse-video block for "this one", and rounded green glass kept for the machine alone. These are cut from dark oxblood Bakelite with warm porcelain type. It should feel warm, quiet and exact, like an old radio at night with its dial lit and one green eye open.
designs.companions: The companion is oxblood Bakelite, moved in this revision from plum (h350-359) to true oxblood (h15-22) at C about 0.025. It is solid material with a job, never a light. It fills every family window (surface #241415), dialog (#2a191a), the family's chat bubbles and the month's event chips (#3c2d2c), checkbox and tick wells (#332323), the bar, the phone strip and the foot (#1a0f10), the frame lines (#4b3939 and #5d4b4a, hairlines #342626, dots #3d2e2e) and the monitor case (#3a2826, one step under the frame lines). Warm porcelain sets the type: ink #d9d3ce, ink-2 #bfb5b0, dim #a69795, faint #988a87 and headings #e9dfdb. Old rose, calmed to #c1a3a5 (h13, 13.3 dE from the pink 'shows'), takes the mono labels, dates, said-by and facts. The block for "this one" is a lit dial-window greige, #ab9a91 with #0d110b ink at 7.0:1. It is used on the bar, the frame-line tabs, the Settings menu, the picker's hover and today's date. On the phone the current place is a raised Bakelite cell with a 2px greige cap. Sage #8fd3a6 takes the links, ticks, the typed-in field and the Status legend icons. Green-black glass (#111812, #131d14, field #111610) holds the greeting, Vera's bubbles and every field. The kinds keep Magic Eye's set: lilac, sky, straw, amber, pink, coral, salmon red. #6dff9c stays on the mark, Send and the primary buttons, "mind", focus rings, the power LEDs, the live lamps and the tubes.
decisions:
Kept from the draft (Reverse Video's structure):
- the masthead and the board of windows
- unboxed strip rows with a tabular mono facts column and dotted hairlines
- the highlight bar that fades over 1s, and reverse video for selection
- double frames only for dialogs, with a dialog's frame turning sage while you type in it (:has(:focus))
- square family surfaces against rounded machine glass, and flush scopes on Status and Ideas
- base-select pickers, 2.75rem targets and both focus-ring fixes
- IBM Plex Sans with Plex Mono, and VT323 only on the tubes

Neutrals moved from aubergine to oxblood (h15-22) and the type from rose-porcelain to warm porcelain, as the critic asked. The page now reads as brown-red Bakelite with ivory type, not green plus pink. Ink stays calm at 12.85:1 on bg. The smallest text (faint) is 5.33:1 on surface and 5.51 on field.

One exception, measured deliberately: the family's bubble is #3c2d2c rather than the suggested #3b2a2a. At #3b2a2a its HSV saturation (0.288) crosses the harness's 'coloured' threshold, and Chat's green share fell from 32% to 16%. #3c2d2c is visually identical, grounded at C 0.022, and brings Chat back to 32.5%.

The case is the same Bakelite as the plates, one step darker than the frame lines (#3a2826). It is also thinner and squarer:
- padding .6rem .6rem 1.9rem
- radius 18/18/22/22, and 12px/14px on the tube
- vents and the green power LED moved down to the new chin
- sheen warmed to #ffeee6
The flush scopes on Status and Ideas are now 14px and 8px.

Status lamps are now a jewelled pilot lamp, the radio's other green light: .8rem, a radial highlight to a deep green edge, a 1.5px dark bezel ring and an 8px glow. I tried the critic's magic-eye conic-wedge lamp first. At 13px, with its dark centre cap, it read as a keyhole or padlock, which is the wrong message for 'working'.

Every name in the frame line now straddles the line on every page. The legend is lifted with top:-.6rem on its position:relative box instead of a negative top margin, which collapsed through block panels. The same fix applies to section heads and tabs, and reset rules keep dialogs' own legend margin intact.

One typographic system for small caps: a --caps token (500 .75rem/1.3 Plex Mono) is shared by eyebrows, month headers, table headers and captions, counts, date-tile caps, filter labels and the ask box's FROM. Tracking is .03em everywhere (legends and tabs too), since the face is already monospaced. Field labels stay sentence-case Plex Sans. One-word bar labels are the only mono-caps labels.

To do became one window: the Show/Search/Filter toolbar is the tray's first line under a hairline, and the lone glyph legend is gone. The 'Open' tag is a quiet outlined printed tag. The reminder line is a mono fact in label rose, and 'Edit, complete, or snooze' shares its line, so rows went from about 110px to about 89px. DOM and Tab order are unchanged.

The Plans month now reads correctly:
- weekends a shade lighter (7% greige over the plate)
- days outside the month switched off (70% green-black)
- no shade on the header cells
- event chips raised Bakelite with the 2px sky rule
- today in reverse video, so amber keeps its one job ('needs a look')

Declined: moving 'outing' away from the sage links. Every outing that clears the links by 7 dE or more falls under the colour-blind floor against 'activity' (protan 0.2-3.4, against 6.4 now). Every accent that clears outing is a greyed sage that reads less like a link. The two share a window only on Home's Lately added, and there the link is underlined and set in the frame line.

PLANS month: the weekend shading and the outside-month days are the same colour. Fix: `table.month td.outside{background:var(--bg)}` with faint numerals (the switched-off screen), a lighter weekend `table.month td:nth-child(n+6){background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--rev) 7%,var(--win))}`, and no shade on th.
